signals.topic: Prompt caching writes additional cache entries past explicit breakpoint, overbilling users 1.25x for tokens never read
signals.summary: When users set a single explicit cache_control breakpoint on the system block (not using automatic caching), the server writes an additional ~1416-token cache entry on every warm call past that breakpoint. These writes are billed at 1.25x cache-write rate but never produce any cache_read on subsequent calls, since no additional breakpoint exists and trailing content varies per request. Users have no documented opt-out mechanism.
aliases: extra cache writes on explicit breakpoint
signals.review_reason: Direct financial harm: users are charged 1.25x cache-write rate for tokens that are never read back on any subsequent call. The behavior contradicts published documentation which states only the marked breakpoint produces a cache entry. No opt-out mechanism exists, so every warm call using explicit caching incurs unrecoupable cost. This is a clear cost-loss pain point.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Server writes additional cache entries past explicit `cache_control` breakpoint, billing 1.25x for tokens that are never read
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed reproducible with exact token counts across Call 1/2/3. Call 2 and 3 each write ~1416 extra cache tokens billed at 1.25x with zero cache_read benefit. No opt-out mechanism exists. Users paying real money for tokens that provide zero value.

signals.topic: MCP connector intermittently emits tool_use instead of mcp_tool_use for declared MCP tools, forcing workaround and extra round-trips
signals.summary: Under the mcp-client-2025-11-20 beta connector, the model occasionally returns a plain tool_use block for a tool name declared in an mcp_toolset config (with enabled: true), instead of the expected mcp_tool_use block. No server-side execution occurs, conversation stalls without a tool_result, and subsequent turns often correct themselves. Users must implement a workaround that detects server-managed tool names and sends a placeholder tool_result, costing an extra round-trip and wasted tokens per occurrence.
aliases: mcp_toolset emits tool_use instead of mcp_tool_use
signals.review_reason: Non-blocking but significant UX degradation: conversations stall mid-loop without the documented mcp_tool_use behavior, forcing users to implement defensive detection-and-placeholder workarounds that add latency and burn tokens. The MCP connector is a core beta feature; its intermittent misrouting undermines trust in the feature for production agentic workflows.

source_issues.title: [BUG] MCP connector: model intermittently emits tool_use instead of mcp_tool_use for tools declared in mcp_toolset
source_issues.evidence: Conversation stalls without placeholder tool_result workaround. Each occurrence burns extra tokens on the misrouted call plus one additional round-trip. Observed in multi-turn agentic loops with context-management edits active. Not deterministic to reproduce but directly impacts reliability of MCP-backed agent workflows.

signals.topic: Managed Agents: vault_ids not inherited by subagents dispatched via agent_toolset, breaking OAuth-backed MCP tool calls
signals.summary: When a coordinator agent dispatches a subagent using agent_toolset_20260401, the vault credentials configured via vault_ids at sessions.create are not available to the subagent's execution context. Any MCP tool call in the subagent requiring OAuth credentials (e.g. Dynamics 365, Microsoft Graph MCP servers) fails with an auth error. The agent_toolset tool accepts no vault_ids parameter, and there is no inheritance mechanism. The only workaround is manual multi-session orchestration, which defeats the purpose of agent_toolset and loses the unified event stream.
aliases: vault credentials not passed to subagents in multi-agent setup
signals.review_reason: Key vault-credential integration is fundamentally broken for the primary multi-agent orchestration pattern. Users following the official managed agents + vault documentation find their OAuth-backed MCP tools silently fail in subagent contexts, with no error that points to the root cause. The workaround (manual multi-session orchestration) discards the entire benefit of the agent_toolset abstraction.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents: vault_ids not inherited by subagents dispatched via agent_toolset — MCP OAuth calls fail
source_issues.evidence: Vault credentials + managed agents is the documented secure pattern for connecting agents to external services. The moment a coordinator/subagent split is introduced (primary use case for agent_toolset_20260401), vault-backed MCP tools stop working for all non-coordinator agents. Multi-agent pipelines requiring OAuth-backed MCP calls from subagents are effectively blocked.

signals.topic: Managed Agents: all Claude models rejected with 'model is not supported' on sessions.create and agents.create
signals.summary: All Claude 4.5+ models are rejected with 'model is not supported' error on both agents.create() and sessions.create() via the Managed Agents beta API, even though the same models work perfectly on the Messages API with the same API key. Agent creation succeeded earlier the same day, but all subsequent calls fail. Sessions.create for existing agents also fails with the same error. Both cloud and self-hosted environments are affected.
aliases: Managed Agents model rejection all models fail
signals.review_reason: Complete main-flow blockage for all Managed Agents users: both agents.create and sessions.create fail for every Claude model, while the same models work on the Messages API. This is not a partial degradation — it renders the entire Managed Agents beta unusable for affected users. The issue is confirmed reproducible and is_recently_active.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents: "model is not supported" for all models on sessions.create and agents.create
source_issues.evidence: All Claude 4.x models rejected with 400 BadRequestError. Same API key and same models work on Messages API. Both sessions.create and agents.create blocked. Affects all cloud and self-hosted environments. Per documentation, all Claude 4.5+ models should be supported.

signals.topic: Official tool_runner 'advanced usage' docs example causes infinite loop due to append_messages in loop body
signals.summary: The 'Advanced usage' example in the official Anthropic tool_runner documentation calls runner.append_messages(user_message) inside the tool runner loop. This sets _messages_modified = True, which causes __run__ to skip auto-appending the assistant message + tool result. The next iteration sends a request with no tool result in history, so Claude sees the original question unanswered and makes the tool call again, creating an infinite loop. The 'Modifying tool results' example on the same page correctly passes both the message and tool_response, which is the working pattern.
aliases: beta_tool runner docs example infinite loop
signals.review_reason: Critical DX failure: the official 'advanced usage' documentation example causes an infinite loop, completely blocking the primary tool_runner usage pattern. Users who follow the docs get trapped in an infinite loop with no indication of what went wrong. This is a high-confidence bug with a clear root cause — the _messages_modified flag interaction — confirmed by the reporter and contrasting with the adjacent 'Modifying tool results' example that uses the correct pattern.

source_issues.title: [Bug] append_messages() inside tool runner loop causes infinite loop (advanced usage docs example)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: _messages_modified flag causes __run__ to skip auto-append of tool results. Infinite loop confirmed. The bug is in the official documentation example itself, not user code. Users following the official docs will hit this blocking issue.

signals.topic: Bundled CLI prompt cache never reads in multi-turn headless runs, causing 429 rate limit errors and 3x cost
signals.summary: In multi-turn headless SDK runs, the bundled Claude Code CLI creates prompt cache on every turn but never reads it (cache_read_input_tokens=0 across all turns). This causes the third turn to hit per-minute input-token rate limits (429) and costs 3x the expected amount. The direct anthropic Python SDK over the same endpoint shows healthy cache reads, confirming the bug is in the bundled CLI. Root cause is likely per-turn dynamic injection into the system block, tool-array reordering, or cache_control breakpoint placement drift.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow regression that directly causes 429 rate limit errors and ~3x cost inflation in multi-turn agentic runs. The evidence includes a minimal repro showing cache_read=0 vs the healthy direct-SDK probe (cache_read=2722 on turn 2). Count=1 but P0 is warranted because the impact is severe (rate limit blocking + cost) and the root cause (bundled CLI per-turn system-block mutation defeating cache prefix match) is a core failure in the most fundamental SDK workflow.

source_issues.title: Bundled CLI never reads prompt cache in multi-turn headless runs (direct anthropic SDK over the same endpoint caches correctly)
source_issues.evidence: cache_create_input_tokens=45781 per turn, cache_read_input_tokens=0 across all turns; third turn trips 429; direct anthropic SDK probe shows healthy cache reads proving the issue is bundled CLI-side. Reported in both SDK v0.1.81 and v0.2.82 across multiple turns.

signals.topic: Query.close() does not reap MCP subprocess grandchildren, causing resource leak
signals.summary: When ClaudeSDKClient.query() is closed, the transport.close() only terminates the CLI subprocess but leaves its MCP server child processes running. These grandchildren reparent to PID 1 and persist until the parent Python process exits. Over long-running processes with many query dispatches, this causes OOM, file-descriptor exhaustion, and CPU burn.
signals.review_reason: This is a resource leak in the SDK's core query lifecycle. While count=1, the impact is severe: each query dispatch with MCP servers leaks one child process per server, leading to OOM and file-descriptor exhaustion over time. Long-running pipelines and daemons are directly affected. The reproduction is deterministic with a full minimal repro provided, and the source-level root cause is identified in SubprocessCLITransport.close().

source_issues.title: Query.close() does not reap MCP subprocess grandchildren
source_issues.evidence: MCP server subprocesses reparent to PID 1 and persist after Query.close(). Full reproduction script provided showing leak after single query dispatch. Source code trace shows SubprocessCLITransport.close() never enumerates children or calls killpg. Affects both macOS and Linux across SDK 0.1.63-0.1.68.

signals.topic: TaskNotificationMessage fires before subagent has finished executing (race condition)
signals.summary: When an orchestrator dispatches multiple subagents in parallel via the Task tool, the SDK sometimes delivers TaskNotificationMessage to the orchestrator while the referenced subagent is still actively executing tool calls. The notification arrives 76-850 seconds before the actual TASK_DONE/ResultMessage. This causes the orchestrator to prematurely dispatch downstream agents against output files that don't exist yet.
signals.review_reason: This causes incorrect orchestrator behavior where downstream agents are dispatched against non-existent files due to premature completion signals. The cascade impact is severe: wasted re-dispatches, stale notification floods, and doubled run costs. Even though count=1 and non-deterministic, the operational impact is clear from the provided timeline and log evidence, making this a P1.

source_issues.title: TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running (premature, not cross-turn leak)
source_issues.evidence: Non-deterministic but reproducible (1 of 2 identical runs). Timeline shows <task-notification> arriving while subagent is still at tool=13 of 39. Orchestrator dispatches reviewers against non-existent files. Cascade: 5 reviewers dispatched prematurely, 5 researchers re-dispatched, total run wasted 32 min / $21.51.

signals.topic: skills='all' does not automatically add 'Skill' to tools list when tools are explicitly defined

The allowed_tools docstring implies it configures everything, but Skill must still be manually added to the tools list.
aliases: skills not working with explicit tools
signals.review_reason: This causes a critical feature (Skills) to silently fail in production, with the failure mode being environment-dependent (works locally, fails in Kubernetes). The documentation is actively misleading ('configure everything' in allowed_tools docstring) and the failure is silent — users spend significant time debugging. Count=1 but P1 due to the non-obvious silent failure and documentation misdirection.

source_issues.title: skills='all' does not add 'Skill' to tools
source_issues.evidence: User spent significant time debugging skills not working in Kubernetes. Skills work locally but fail silently in the cloud environment. Workaround: manually add 'Skill' to the tools list. allowed_tools docstring reads 'configure everything' which is misleading.

signals.summary: When a subagent finishes with a StructuredOutput block followed by additional tool calls, the structured_output field is missing from the returned ResultMessage. The subagent waits for the StructuredOutput block before finishing, but the field is not present in the output.

signals.topic: Native binary (~230MB) exceeds serverless deployment size limits, blocking Vercel/Lambda/Edge use
signals.summary: The Bun-compiled single-executable distribution (~230 MB per platform since v0.2.110) exceeds Vercel's 250 MB function size limit and approaches AWS Lambda's cap, making serverless deployments completely non-functional. This is a deployment-model incompatibility introduced by switching from a ~13 MB JS bundle to a native binary.
aliases: Serverless deployment blocked by binary size
Bun single-executable incompatible with serverless platforms
signals.review_reason: This is a clear deployment blocking issue: the SDK's native binary (~230 MB) cannot fit within Vercel's 250 MB function size cap, making serverless a completely non-viable deployment target. This is a primary deployment path for many embedders and the issue was introduced as a distribution model change (JS bundle → native binary) without a documented serverless alternative.

source_issues.title: Native binary distribution (≥0.2.110) makes Agent SDK unusable in Vercel/Lambda serverless deployments (230 MB pushes past the 250 MB function size cap)
source_issues.evidence: 230 MB binary alone exceeds Vercel's 250 MB function size limit; deployment fails at runtime with 'Native CLI binary for linux-x64 not found'; no documented serverless path exists; ~17x size growth from JS bundle (13 MB → 230 MB) introduced at v0.2.110

signals.topic: Sub-agents cannot access parent's in-process MCP servers, causing silent tool fabrication and incorrect results
signals.summary: When a parent query registers in-process MCP servers via createSdkMcpServer, sub-agent dispatch fails to surface those tools in the sub-agent's runtime tool registry. The model emits tool_call XML as plain text (tool_uses: 0) and fabricates plausible but incorrect results. The root cause is that AgentMcpServerSpec type deliberately excludes the instance variant for sub-agents.
aliases: In-process MCP servers not accessible to sub-agents
Sub-agent mcpServers reference by name silently fails
signals.review_reason: This is a critical workflow-blocking issue: sub-agents in a coordinator-first architecture cannot use in-process MCP servers at all, forcing users to route all MCP calls through the parent loop. The failure is silent (no error, tool_call appears as plain text, fabricated results look plausible) and breaks a core architectural pattern (coordinator-first with MCP-routed sub-agents). The SDK's type system actively prevents a correct configuration.

source_issues.title: Sub-agent AgentDefinition.mcpServers does not surface parent's in-process createSdkMcpServer tools at runtime (SDK 0.3.144)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed by two independent agents in production: sub-agent's response contains <tool_call> XML in plain content with tool_uses: 0 in usage block; identical AgentDefinitions on different hosts produce the same break; SDK's type system (McpServerConfigForProcessTransport) deliberately excludes instance variant for sub-agents; workaround restricts MCP calls to parent loop only, defeating coordinator-first pattern

signals.topic: Isolation flags (mcpServers: {}, settingSources: [], skills: []) do not strip claude.ai connector inventory from system init, causing context bloat and response compaction
signals.summary: Even when all documented isolation flags are set, the SDK's system.init event still ships the operator's full claude.ai connector inventory (87–369 mcp__claude_ai_* tool definitions), agents array, memory_paths.auto, and skills array. This bloats prompts by 200–400 KB, causing Sonnet 4.6 to compact responses before emitting tool_use blocks (compacted_lost_tool_use escalation).
aliases: mcpServers: {} does not strip claude.ai connectors from init
Isolation flags fail to prevent operator context bleed
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking issue: the documented isolation flags fail to deliver their documented contract, causing operator claude.ai connector inventory (up to 370 tools) to leak into bounded SDK calls. This causes observable response compaction (tool_use blocks lost) on bounded sub-agent calls — a primary SDK use case — making the system unreliable for structured-output pipelines.

source_issues.title: Options { mcpServers: {}, settingSources: [], skills: [] } doesn't strip claude.ai-connector tools, agents, or memory_paths.auto from system init (0.2.126)
source_issues.evidence: Observed across 6 runs: 336 total tools (335 mcp__claude_ai_*) when only 1 expected; 6 agents when 0 expected; 8 skills when 0 expected; populated memory_paths.auto; tool count varied 88–370 across runs due to operator's changing connector inventory; Sonnet 4.6 observed compacting response before emitting tool_use blocks due to context pressure (compacted_lost_tool_use escalation reasons); 200–400 KB prompt bloat documented

signals.topic: OTel tracer emits non-GenAI-semconv token attribute names, causing downstream cost tracking to report $0 for all generations
signals.summary: The bundled OTel tracer emits bare token attribute names (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens) instead of OTel GenAI semantic convention names (gen_ai.usage.*). This causes Langfuse and other GenAI-semconv-aware observability backends to show $0 cost for every generation, as they extract cost only from the standard attribute names.
aliases: OTel token attribute names violate GenAI semantic conventions
Tracer emits wrong attribute names causing $0 cost in Langfuse
Non-semconv token attributes break cost tracking
signals.review_reason: This is a significant cost-tracking failure affecting production observability: every generation appears to cost $0 in Langfuse because the tracer emits non-standard attribute names. While pricing on the Anthropic side is unaffected, this means enterprise users relying on Langfuse (or any GenAI-semconv consumer) for cost attribution get silently incorrect data, which could mislead budget decisions and cost allocation across projects.

source_issues.title: Tracer emits non-semconv token attributes (scope com.anthropic.claude_code.tracing v1.0.0) — continuation of #304 with new evidence
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed in Langfuse: every claude_code.llm_request generation shows usage_details: {}, calculated_total_cost: $0.0; spans flow correctly but attribute names diverge from OTel GenAI semconv; cache token rows also diverge on the _input infix, not just the gen_ai.usage. prefix; workaround requires per-project mapping rules that cannot be applied by other GenAI-semconv consumers (Honeycomb, Tempo, custom collectors)

signals.topic: restoreConfigFromBase ENOENT crash on symlinks in .claude/ pointing outside SENSITIVE_PATHS
signals.summary: The restoreConfigFromBase step crashes with ENOENT when .claude/ contains symlinks pointing to directories outside SENSITIVE_PATTS (e.g., .claude/skills/ -> ../../.agents/skills/). Regression introduced by #1186 (dereference: true) + Bun 1.3.14 upgrade on 2026-05-14.
signals.review_reason: Two separate users report the same crash (restoreConfigFromBase ENOENT) with identical root cause: symlinks inside .claude/ that point to paths outside SENSITIVE_PATHS. Both users confirm this is a regression introduced on 2026-05-14 by the combination of the dereference:true fix and Bun 1.3.14. The failure blocks the action entirely at the restore step, preventing any Claude Code execution. Both are open bugs with no resolution.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase ENOENT on .claude/ symlinks whose target is outside SENSITIVE_PATHS (regression after dereference + Bun 1.3.14)

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase crashes on dangling symlinks in .claude/ directory

signals.topic: MCP server termination failure causing workflow to hang indefinitely after Claude completes
signals.summary: After Claude Code completes its task, MCP server processes (bun processes for github_comment and github_ci) are not properly terminated, causing the GitHub Actions workflow to hang indefinitely until manually cancelled or hitting timeout.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed workflow-level blocker. After Claude completes its task successfully and posts its review, the workflow never exits due to orphan MCP server processes. This forces users to manually cancel or wait for timeout, wasting CI resources and blocking downstream jobs. While count=1, the severity is high — the action appears to work (Claude posts) but then blocks the workflow indefinitely, which is a critical UX failure for any automated CI use case.

source_issues.title: MCP servers not terminated after Claude completes - workflow hangs indefinitely
source_issues.evidence: Workflow hangs indefinitely after Claude posts review; logs show orphan bun processes (MCP servers) not terminated at cleanup. User must add timeout-minutes as workaround. Full review posted but workflow never exits.

signals.topic: HTTP MCP server tools not appearing in agent's tool list when --allowedTools wildcard is used
signals.summary: When an HTTP MCP server is declared via .mcp.json and --allowedTools uses a wildcard (e.g., '*'), the MCP server's tools never appear in the Claude agent's available tool list, making MCP servers unusable with wildcard tool permissions.
aliases: mcp tools invisible with wildcard allowedTools
signals.review_reason: MCP server integration is a core feature of claude-code-action. When HTTP MCP servers are declared and --allowedTools uses wildcards, the tools are silently absent from the agent's tool list. This breaks MCP server workflows without clear error messaging. While count=1, the issue is confirmed (closed with bug/dev-experience/mcp labels), making MCP servers fundamentally unusable in this common configuration.

source_issues.title: HTTP MCP server declared via .mcp.json with --allowedTools wildcard: tools never appear in agent's tool list
source_issues.evidence: HTTP MCP server tools not appearing in agent's tool list when .mcp.json declares the server and --allowedTools wildcard is used. This prevents MCP server integration from working, a core feature of the action.

signals.topic: Action crashes on runners without AVX CPU support due to Bun-based build
signals.summary: The Bun-based Claude binary requires AVX CPU instructions, causing the action to crash with 'Illegal instruction' on self-hosted runners or older VPS hardware lacking AVX support. The npm version works fine on the same hardware.
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow failure on affected self-hosted runners. The action crashes immediately with 'Illegal instruction' due to AVX CPU requirement, making it completely unusable on a meaningful subset of self-hosted runners (common on older VPS hardware). The user cannot use the action at all without switching hardware. This is a significant blocker for self-hosted CI users and blocks adoption in organizations with mixed hardware.

source_issues.title: Action fails on runners without AVX CPU support
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes with '748 Illegal instruction bun run' on self-hosted runner without AVX CPU support. The npm version of claude works fine on the same hardware. User's entire self-hosted CI setup is blocked.

signals.topic: File descriptor leak regression in large monorepos (v2.1.143+) causes system freezes, FS corruption, and machine reimaging
signals.summary: A regression introduced in v2.1.143 causes file descriptor leaks when working with large Android/Kotlin monorepos, leading to system freezes requiring hard reboot, Git index corruption, and in severe cases requiring machine reimaging. Multiple developers are affected and the issue was not present in v2.1.126.
signals.review_reason: P0 despite count=1 because the severity is extreme: system freezes requiring hard reboot, file system corruption, and machine reimaging. It is explicitly a regression with confirmed reproduction and multiple developers affected. The FD leak blocks all work on large monorepos, constituting a main-flow failure.

source_issues.title: [BUG] File descriptor leak regression in large monorepos (2.1.143+)
source_issues.evidence: FD leak causes system freezes requiring hard reboot, file system corruption affecting Git index and IDE metadata, and in severe cases developers needed to reimage machines. Multiple developers on large monorepo projects affected. Regression from issue #51933, not present in v2.1.126.

signals.topic: Bash tool returns exit code 127 on every command in v2.1.147 on Linux, making Bash completely unusable
signals.summary: In Claude Code v2.1.147 on Linux, every Bash tool invocation fails with exit code 127 including shell builtins and absolute paths to existing binaries, completely breaking the Bash tool. The issue appears to be upstream of the user's shell (tool wrapper itself).
signals.review_reason: Bash tool completely unusable for all commands on Linux in v2.1.147. Exit 127 fires for builtins and absolute paths, confirming the failure is not shell configuration. This blocks the primary mechanism for code execution and tool use.

source_issues.title: Bash tool returns exit code 127 on every command in 2.1.147
source_issues.evidence: Every Bash invocation fails with exit code 127, including shell builtins (pwd, whoami) and absolute paths to real binaries (/bin/pwd). Bash tool is completely unusable; the failure is in the tool wrapper upstream of the user's shell.

signals.topic: Desktop app hardcodes --permission-mode default; auto mode UI toggle fails with error
signals.summary: When Claude Code is launched via the Claude desktop app, it is started with --permission-mode default hardcoded in process arguments. The UI toggle to switch to auto mode fails with 'Permission mode couldn't be changed. You can try again.' Settings files have no effect because the command-line flag overrides them. Only sessions already in auto mode before this regression continue to work.
aliases: permission mode auto toggle fails desktop
signals.review_reason: Core permission feature blocked for desktop app users on Max plan. Auto mode is a key capability that users pay for; the regression means the UI toggle is non-functional and settings files are ignored. Newly initiated sessions are permanently stuck in default mode.

source_issues.title: Desktop app launches claude with --permission-mode default hardcoded; auto mode toggle fails
source_issues.evidence: Desktop app v1.8555.0 passes --permission-mode default explicitly on launch. UI toggle to auto mode fails with an error message. Settings files (~/.claude/settings.json) have no effect because CLI flags override them. Max plan users cannot enable auto mode for newly initiated sessions.

signals.topic: Lone UTF-16 surrogate in model output corrupts session JSONL file, all subsequent turns fail with 400
signals.summary: A single unpaired UTF-16 surrogate code unit emitted by the model gets persisted into the project JSONL session file, after which every subsequent turn in that session fails with API Error 400 'no low surrogate in string'. The only recovery is /clear, but non-technical users may lose hours of context.
aliases: lone surrogate code unit breaks session
signals.review_reason: Session permanently breaks after a single model output containing an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate. All subsequent turns fail with 400 and the only recovery (/clear) causes context loss. This is a silent, catastrophic data integrity failure.

source_issues.title: Lone UTF-16 surrogate in assistant output bricks session with 400 'no low surrogate'
source_issues.evidence: A single unpaired UTF-16 surrogate code unit emitted by the model is persisted into the project JSONL session file, causing every subsequent turn to fail with API Error 400 'no low surrogate in string'. Only /clear recovers; non-technical users lose hours of context. Reproduced on Opus 4.7, 1M-context build, macOS.

signals.topic: Multi-image upload in single message triggers cache_control 400 error, permanently breaks session
signals.summary: When attaching multiple images to a single message in Claude Code on the web, the session can permanently break with API Error 400 'cache_control cannot be set for empty text blocks'. Once triggered, every subsequent message in that session returns the same 400 because the corrupted content block is replayed in conversation history.
aliases: cache_control empty text blocks web session break
signals.review_reason: Uploading multiple images permanently breaks the web session with no recovery path other than starting over. Every subsequent message fails with 400 because the corrupted block is replayed. Clear user-impacting session destruction.

source_issues.title: [BUG] API Error 400 'cache_control cannot be set for empty text blocks' — triggered by multi-image upload in single message
source_issues.evidence: Multi-image upload in a single message creates a corrupted content block with an empty text block that has cache_control set. This permanently breaks the session — every subsequent message replays the corrupted block and returns 400. Session cannot recover without starting over.

signals.topic: Summarization cookbook uses deprecated assistant message prefill, causing BadRequestError at runtime
signals.summary: The summarization cookbook (capabilities/summarization/guide.ipynb) uses assistant message prefill which is now a deprecated/unsupported API feature. Running cell 8 triggers a BadRequestError with message 'This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.', making the notebook entirely unusable for users who try to follow it.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed runtime failure: the official summarization cookbook crashes with a BadRequestError on cell 8 due to a deprecated API feature (assistant message prefill). A user attempted to run the notebook end-to-end and was blocked. This is a primary use case (learning to build a summarization pipeline) that is completely broken. While count=1 and single-repo, the evidence is unambiguous and the user impact is direct and blocking — not speculative.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Summarization cookbook fails due to use of assistant message prefill
source_issues.evidence: Full BadRequestError traceback provided. Cell 8 calls basic_summarize() which passes an assistant role message as prefill. API returns 400: 'This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.' Notebook is completely blocked — user cannot complete the tutorial without fixing the code.

signals.topic: Plugins crash on non-English Windows locales due to implicit UTF-8 assumption
signals.summary: skill-creator's init_skill.py crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on Windows with cp1252 locale when printing emojis or writing the → character to SKILL.md. hookify's config_loader.py and rule_engine.py silently drop all rule files with UnicodeDecodeError on Korean cp949 locale. hookify's config_loader.py also crashes on Python 3.8 with PEP 585 generics evaluated at import time. These are distinct but related: all stem from implicit encoding/version assumptions that fail on non-POSIX or older Python environments.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：skill-creator和hookify在非英文Windows或Python 3.8环境下直接崩溃，插件完全无法使用。3条独立issue均来自真实用户报告，明确可复现。这是生态系统的跨平台兼容性问题。

source_issues.title: skill-creator: init_skill.py crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on Windows (cp1252)
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeEncodeError on Windows cp1252 when printing emojis and writing → character. sys.stdout uses locale encoding without explicit utf-8 reconfigure.

source_issues.title: hookify: UTF-8 encoding fix needed for Korean Windows (cp949)
source_issues.evidence: hookify silently drops all rule files on Korean cp949 locale. UnicodeDecodeError from reading UTF-8 files with cp949 fallback.

source_issues.title: hookify: config_loader.py crashes on Python 3.8 -- uses PEP 585 generics without future import or version pin
source_issues.evidence: TypeError on Python 3.8: 'type' object is not subscriptable for tuple[...], dict[...] annotations evaluated at import time. No version pin. Common on macOS.

signals.topic: Plugins show 'Published' in Console but are not discoverable in the marketplace
signals.summary: Plugins vibe-radar and Claude Code Inspect both show 'Published' status in the Console (since Apr 14, 2026 for vibe-radar) but are not present in marketplace.json or claude.com/plugins search. /plugin install returns 'not found'. Users cannot discover or install plugins that the Console claims are published.
aliases: plugin published but not in marketplace
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：Console显示'Published'但用户无法找到或安装插件，导致开发者困惑并浪费调试时间。存在Console状态与实际 marketplace 的同步gap，影响插件发布工作流。

source_issues.title: vibe-radar shows 'Published' in Console but not present in claude-plugins-official directory
source_issues.evidence: vibe-radar published since Apr 14 but not in marketplace.json, not at claude.com/plugins search, /plugin install returns not found.

source_issues.title: My submission published but i can't find it anywhere?!
source_issues.evidence: Claude Code Inspect shows Published in Console but not in marketplace or GitHub org. User confused about publishing workflow.

signals.topic: Discord plugin: session respawns cause IDENTIFY-storm and bot token revocation
signals.summary: Discord plugin has no single-instance lock or IDENTIFY rate-limiting. When Claude Code sessions restart frequently (automation, multiple sessions, or silent failures), each fresh session spawns a fresh plugin subprocess that calls client.login(), exhausting Discord's 1000 IDENTIFY/24h limit. Discord then auto-resets the bot token, permanently killing the bot with no warning.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Discord bot token被永久撤销，bot下线，用户必须手动重置token并重新配置才能恢复。影响所有使用restart automation、多个CC session、或遇到silent failures的用户。非边缘场景。

source_issues.title: discord: IDENTIFY-storm class of bug — bot token reset when CC sessions respawn frequently
source_issues.evidence: Discord auto-reset bot token after >1000 IDENTIFY connections/24h. Email confirmed enforcement. Plugin has no single-instance lock or IDENTIFY budget tracking. Any user with restart automation, multiple sessions, or silent failures is exposed.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: orphaned bun subprocess survives parent exit; infinite retry loop burns 99% CPU
signals.summary: Telegram plugin's onStart hook resets the retry attempt counter to 0, defeating the 409 Conflict exit clause. This creates an infinite retry loop consuming 99% CPU when two Claude Code sessions share the same bot token. Additionally, bun subprocesses survive their parent CC process on ungraceful exit, becoming zombies that hold the bot token.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：无限重试循环导致CPU 99%占用，Telegram bot实质上不可用；zombie进程持有bot token导致无法正常重启恢复。用户体验显著下降且难以自行诊断。

source_issues.title: telegram@0.0.6: orphaned bun process holds bot token, retry loop exit clause defeated by onStart reset
source_issues.evidence: onStart in grammY resets retry counter to 0, defeating 8-conflict exit clause → infinite retry loop burning 99% CPU. bun subprocess survives parent CC process (zombie bot). .in_use/ marker files leak on ungraceful exit.

signals.topic: security-guidance plugin: state file race condition causes security warnings to be re-shown
signals.summary: security_reminder_hook.py writes session-keyed state to JSON files without file locking (flock) or atomic write operations. Under concurrent PreToolUse hook fires within a single session, two writers race and lose entries, causing security warnings to be re-displayed when they should have been suppressed.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：security hook的核心功能（压制已显示的安全警告）失效，用户反复看到相同的安全警告，体验显著下降。这是数据丢失类race condition，可复现。

source_issues.title: security-guidance: state file race condition (no flock, no atomic write)
source_issues.evidence: security_reminder_hook.py writes JSON state without flock or atomic write. Concurrent PreToolUse hook fires cause lost writes → security warnings re-shown when they should be suppressed. Includes acceptance test design proving the race.

signals.topic: README advertises Python 3.8+ but code requires Python 3.10+ causing TypeError on import
signals.summary: The README states Python 3.8+ as the minimum requirement, but the codebase uses PEP 604 union syntax (X | None) and PEP 585 generics (list[...]) which are only supported in Python 3.10+. Users following the README and running on Python 3.8/3.9 encounter a TypeError immediately on import of the agent module, blocking the main use case of running the quickstart.
aliases: TypeError on import due to wrong Python version in README
signals.review_reason: This is a startup crash: users who follow the documented requirements (Python 3.8+) encounter a TypeError immediately upon importing the agent module. The main use case of the quickstart is blocked for any user running Python 3.8 or 3.9, which is a common LTS version. The issue has clear reproduction steps, affected code references, and a concrete suggested fix. Confidence is 0.75 because only one issue was found for this topic (count=1), limiting generalizability, but the user impact evidence (startup crash on following docs) is unambiguous.

source_issues.title: agents/README.md states "Python 3.8+" but code requires Python 3.10+ (PEP 604 union syntax)
source_issues.evidence: Code uses PEP 604 union syntax (X | None) and PEP 585 generics (list[...]) in runtime-evaluated annotations without 'from __future__ import annotations', causing TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for | on Python 3.8/3.9. CI runs Python 3.11.6. Users following the README on Python 3.8/3.9 hit the error immediately on 'from agents.agent import Agent', blocking the main use case.

signals.topic: Tutorial uses outdated/incompatible API models, blocking user learning
signals.summary: 用户尝试使用较新的 Claude 模型 API 时教程无法正常工作，主流程阻断，无法完成学习目标

source_issues.title: I Can't get it to take my API
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确表示无法选择最新引擎导致 API 无法工作，教程认为需要更新，用户希望使用但被阻断。核心学习流程完全无法进行。

signals.topic: skill-creator description-optimization loop produces 0% recall across all iterations, making skill description tuning non-functional
signals.summary: When running scripts/run_loop.py against a skill with a slash-command name, every iteration scores precision=100%, recall=0%, accuracy=50% regardless of description changes. The candidate skill is registered with a hash-suffixed name (<skill-name>-skill-<hash>), so the judge subprocess cannot find it — the evaluation loop produces no usable optimization signal.
aliases: skill tuning loop produces no signal
signals.review_reason: The optimization loop is structurally broken: the hash-renamed candidate skill cannot be invoked by its original slash-command name, so recall is pinned at 0% across all iterations. Users who rely on this loop to tune skill descriptions have no usable signal and cannot improve their skills. Secondary issue: SessionEnd hook timeouts cause RuntimeError under load, aborting entire runs. This is a primary workflow failure.

source_issues.title: skill-creator description-optimisation loop: recall=0% on every iteration, including literal slash-command queries
source_issues.evidence: Every iteration scores precision=100%, recall=0%, accuracy=50% identically regardless of description content changes. Literal slash-command queries like /triage-issue 67 fail all 3 samples (expected True, got FAIL). The judge cannot locate the hash-renamed candidate skill.

signals.topic: Skills referencing platform-unavailable tools fail silently with no error, causing cross-platform behavioral divergence
signals.summary: When a SKILL.md references a tool that doesn't exist on the running platform (e.g., Claude.ai-only tools on Claude Code, or vice versa), Claude falls back to prose or silently substitutes a tool with different semantics. No error is surfaced, leaving skill authors with no signal that their skill ran differently than intended.
signals.review_reason: This causes silent behavioral divergence across platforms. A skill tested on Claude Code may silently produce wrong results on Claude.ai (or vice versa) without any error — the overwrite semantics difference means data loss or blocking errors depending on platform. Skill authors have zero signal that their skill ran differently, making cross-platform skill development untestable from one platform. This is a critical trust and reliability failure for multi-platform skills.

source_issues.title: Skills referencing tools that don't exist on the running platform fail silently
source_issues.evidence: 6 of 7 Claude.ai-only tools (ask_user_input_v0, image_search, conversation_search, recent_chats, present_files, visualize:show_widget) produced no error when run on Claude Code — fell back to prose silently. Claude.ai substituted Write with create_file which has opposite overwrite semantics (Write overwrites; create_file refuses with 'File already exists'). No error surfaced in either direction.

signals.topic: references/ relative paths in SKILL.md don't resolve from the skill's own directory, breaking the documented progressive-disclosure pattern
signals.summary: The skill-creator skill's recommended references/ progressive-disclosure pattern fails because neither Claude.ai's view nor Claude Code's Read resolves relative paths from the skill's directory. Paths are resolved against the process cwd instead, causing 'File does not exist' errors for skills that reference their own files.
aliases: references/ path not resolving from skill dir
signals.review_reason: The skill-creator explicitly recommends the references/ progressive-disclosure pattern, yet it is fundamentally broken on both major platforms. Skills that follow this documented pattern will fail at runtime with 'File does not exist' or 'not an absolute path'. This is a documented feature that is broken by design, causing authors to hit errors when following official guidance.

source_issues.title: references/ relative paths don't resolve from the skill's directory
source_issues.evidence: Skill at ~/.claude/skills/path-test/ with references/spec.md: Claude Code produces 'File does not exist. Note: your current working directory is /Users/<user>/Documents/<project>' when reading references/spec.md. Claude.ai rejects relative paths outright: 'references/spec.md is not an absolute path.' The 'Base directory for this skill' header injected by Claude Code is informational only and does not affect resolution.

signals.topic: pptx skill produces .pptx files with OOXML compliance issues that fail to import into Apple Keynote on macOS
signals.summary: python-pptx generated .pptx files produced by the pptx skill cannot be imported into Apple Keynote on macOS, failing silently with 'The file format is invalid'. The same files open fine in Microsoft PowerPoint, PowerPoint Online, and LibreOffice, so the failure is silent and only surfaces when a Mac user opens the file. Three OOXML structural bugs are identified: contradictory slide size type attribute, missing notesMasterIdLst, and a Windows-only printer settings stub.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear output quality failure: the skill produces files that cannot be opened on a major platform (macOS/Keynote). The failure is silent — the file appears valid in PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and PowerPoint Online — so Mac users only discover the issue when they try to open the file directly. No error is surfaced at generation time. All Cowork users on macOS are impacted when their workflow involves Keynote, with no recourse other than manual workarounds.

source_issues.title: pptx skill produces .pptx files that fail to import into Apple Keynote (silent OOXML compliance issues)
source_issues.evidence: Files produced by python-pptx via the pptx skill fail with 'Das Dateiformat ist ungültig' (file format invalid) in Apple Keynote. The failure is silent until a Mac user opens the file. OneDrive round-trip (upload → download) corrects the file because PowerPoint Online sanitizes it, confirming the bug is in the skill's output. The workarounds (upload to OneDrive or run a manual sanitizer) are non-obvious and impose friction on all Mac users in Cowork mode.

signals.topic: docx skill uses incorrect Chinese quotation marks ([ ]) in generated documents instead of standard curved quotes ("")
signals.summary: When editing docx files, the docx skill does not use proper Chinese-style quotation marks as required in Chinese-language documents. The skill uses square brackets [ ] instead of the correct curved quotation marks " ", producing documents that fail to meet Chinese typographic standards.
signals.review_reason: The docx skill produces documents with incorrect typographic characters — using square brackets instead of proper curved quotation marks required for Chinese-language documents. While not a crash or data loss, it produces output that fails professional typographic standards and requires manual correction. This is an output content quality defect.

source_issues.title: 编辑docx时会在需要" "的场景不使用" ",而用[ ]替代
source_issues.evidence: The docx skill generates documents using [ ] characters where Chinese curved quotation marks " " are required. The user explicitly provided a SKILL.md instructing the model to use " " but the skill still produces [ ] instead.

signals.topic: DeepSeek V4 provider integration broken — models unusable and multi-turn conversations fail with 400 errors
signals.summary: After DeepSeek released V4, the goose provider still serves V3 model names, exposes wrong 128K context limit instead of 1M, and fails with 400 errors on multi-turn conversations due to unhandled reasoning_content field.
signals.review_reason: The DeepSeek provider is completely broken for V4. Users cannot use DeepSeek V4 models at all — provider serves wrong model names, wrong context limits, and multi-turn conversations (a core workflow) fail with 400 errors on every second message. This is a direct, high-impact block on the main workflow for DeepSeek users.

source_issues.title: DeepSeek V4 update breaks provider — unable to use V4 models
source_issues.evidence: Provider serves V3 model names (deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner), wrong 128K context limit, and multi-turn conversations always get 400 error on second message due to unhandled reasoning_content field.

signals.topic: Tokio multi-threaded runtime silently kills stdio MCP subprocesses between tool calls — causes Transport closed errors
signals.summary: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG with multi-threaded Tokio runtime causes MCP subprocesses to silently die when spawning threads are recycled. Tool calls return -32603 Transport closed errors mid-conversation, completely blocking MCP tool usage.
signals.review_reason: MCP tools are a core feature of goose and this bug causes them to silently die mid-session with opaque Transport closed errors, completely blocking any workflow that relies on stdio MCP servers. The root cause is well-understood and reproducible, affecting all users on multi-threaded Tokio runtime.

source_issues.title: configure_parent_death_signal (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM) silently kills stdio MCP subprocesses on multi-threaded Tokio runtime
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG delivered when spawning thread exits, not parent. Tokio recycles worker threads, delivering SIGTERM to MCP children. Subsequent tool calls return -32603: Transport closed. 1 comment confirms severity.

signals.topic: Embedded MCP app display stuck at 'Waiting for data...' — visualizations and apps never render
signals.summary: Post v1.34.1 upgrade, the embedded MCP app display in the desktop UI shows indefinite loading state and never renders visualizations or apps. The same content renders correctly in a new window, isolating the issue to the embedded display component.
signals.review_reason: Key visualization and app rendering is completely broken in the embedded MCP display mode after a recent update. Users lose the ability to view rich content inline in the desktop UI. The workaround (new window) exists but defeats the embedded experience purpose. This is a clear UX regression that blocks the primary use of visualization apps.

source_issues.title: Embedded MCP App Display Not Rendering - 'Waiting for data...' Stuck State
source_issues.evidence: Steps to reproduce clearly documented. Issue occurs post-upgrade to v1.34.1 on macOS. Same content renders in new window — bug is isolated to embedded display component. 1 comment confirms.

signals.topic: Context window percentage and compact option removed from desktop UI — users lost critical token visibility
signals.summary: After a recent update, the context window percentage number disappeared from the token box in the desktop UI. Users previously relied on this to monitor token usage and decide when to compact. The data is still transmitted internally but the UI no longer displays it.
signals.review_reason: Context window percentage is a critical UX feature users depend on to monitor token usage and prevent context overflow. Its removal is a clear regression that degrades the user experience by removing visibility into a key system metric. While not workflow-blocking, it materially reduces the ability to manage context effectively.

source_issues.title: No context window percentage any more
source_issues.evidence: Goose agent confirmed data is still transmitted in background — pure UI regression. User lost ability to monitor token usage and trigger compaction manually. Affects all providers. Reported by user who relied on this feature daily.

signals.topic: Telegram gateway hardcodes GATEWAY_MAX_TURNS to 5 — cannot be overridden, blocks longer automated sessions
signals.summary: The Telegram gateway has a hardcoded GATEWAY_MAX_TURNS = 5 constant that cannot be overridden by GOOSE_MAX_TURNS or any config.yaml setting. Telegram sessions always stop after exactly 5 LLM turns, preventing users from running longer automated workflows through the Telegram integration.
signals.review_reason: Telegram gateway users cannot run automated sessions longer than 5 turns regardless of configuration. This directly blocks power users who rely on Telegram automation for extended workflows. The hardcoded value makes the GOOSE_MAX_TURNS setting ineffective for an entire integration channel.

source_issues.title: Telegram gateway: GATEWAY_MAX_TURNS hardcoded to 5 — cannot be overridden by GOOSE_MAX_TURNS or any config
source_issues.evidence: Hardcoded constant in crates/goose/src/gateway/handler.rs line 319. GOOSE_MAX_TURNS=9999 has zero effect on Telegram gateway. Bot stops after exactly 5 turns with 'maximum number of actions' message.

signals.topic: browse CLI headed mode steals window focus on every command, interrupting developer workflow
signals.summary: When running `browse` CLI in `--headed` mode on macOS, every command (snapshot, click, get url, etc.) causes the Chromium window to steal focus from the user's active application, breaking the primary use case of running browser automation in parallel with a coding agent.
aliases: headless flag missing local launch options
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user experience pain point: the headed mode focus-stealing directly breaks the primary advertised use case (AI coding agent driving browser automation in parallel). The user explicitly states the workflow is 'interrupted' on every command. While count=1 means it cannot reach P0, it is not a feature request — it is a real DX-breaking behavior that differentiates stagehand's browse CLI unfavorably from Playwright's own headed mode. The issue provides clear reproduction context, root cause analysis (localBrowserLaunchOptions lacks additional Chromium args), and proposed fixes.

source_issues.title: browse CLI: headed mode steals window focus on every command

Playwright itself does not have this issue — it avoids focus-stealing via Chrome flags like --disable-background-timer-throttling and avoids bringToFront() calls.

signals.topic: File upload workflow - uploaded files not visible or not accessible in conversation
signals.summary: User uploads file successfully but file is not visible in conversation page after upload completes, OR file has 600 permissions making it inaccessible to read_file tool in sandbox. Workflow is blocked - files are uploaded but not usable.
signals.review_reason: User workflow is blocked — files are uploaded but not usable. Issue 3132 shows files not visible in UI (experience degradation); Issue 3127 shows files not readable due to permissions (main flow failure). Both directly prevent the file from being used in subsequent steps.

source_issues.title: 文件上传成功后在对话页面看不到上传的文件

signals.topic: Plan/search loop continues after sufficient information gathered, burning excess tokens
signals.summary: Model issues many web_search/web_fetch calls after reasoning indicates enough information has been collected. No final answer produced before manual interruption. Token usage reached ~200K class with no output.
signals.review_reason: Direct cost loss — model continues searching after having enough information, burning tokens without producing final answer. User gets no result after significant token spend. Clear financial impact.

signals.summary: TypeError: 'AsyncCallbackManager' object is not iterable in task_tool.py prevents subagent results from propagating. Subagent tokens=0 in accounting. Lead agent falls back to repeating work.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure in Ultra mode — subagent work is wasted because result cannot be delivered to parent. Clear latency increase and token waste as lead agent repeats subagent's work.

signals.review_reason: Clear cost loss mechanism — failed tool calls echo large error content back into context, causing token usage to multiply across retries. User cost becomes unpredictable and significantly higher than expected.

source_issues.evidence: write_file failures echo ~23-24K char error payloads back into conversation state. Token usage grew from normal to 73799 tokens in observed case. Tool error echoing causes subsequent calls to have much larger input context.

signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker — database errors cause UI to show incorrect run status (still running when actually complete). Users cannot trust the persistence layer; key feature of tracking run history is unreliable.

Cancel button unresponsive during task execution
UI becomes unresponsive blocking all workflow

signals.topic: API errors / interruptions during long sessions leave files in partially edited, corrupted state instead of reverting cleanly

API interruption leaves partially edited files
File reversion fails after API error during edit operations
signals.review_reason: API errors during file edits cause data corruption rather than clean reversion. Users lose trust in the edit safety guarantee and face manual recovery work. Multiple independent reports confirm the pattern in long sessions.

Bedrock profile auth fails with credential_process
AWS SDK credential_process path broken in cline CLI

Bearer token header authentication fails in cline CLI
cline CLI auth regression with OpenAI-compatible provider

signals.topic: JetBrains plugin: terminal output not readable, causing Cline to silently fail terminal commands (e.g. file deletion)

File operations like 'del' fail silently and the task cannot complete.
aliases: JetBrains terminal capture failure causes silent command failure
Terminal output unreadable in IntelliJ prevents task completion

signals.topic: Apply button silently fails to apply code changes in agent mode (Python diffs / hotkey conflict)
signals.summary: The Apply button (or ALT+A hotkey) fails to actually apply code changes in agent mode. In Python files the highlight briefly appears then disappears with no edit applied. In hotkey scenarios it causes UI flicker and wastes tokens. Core editing workflow is broken.
aliases: code diff not applied in agent mode
signals.review_reason: Two distinct reports of the Apply button failing to apply edits in agent mode. One is Python-specific silent failure (no edit applied but no error shown), the other is hotkey conflict causing flicker and token waste. Both directly block the core editing workflow and result in wasted LLM calls. High confidence due to specific technical details and screenshots.

source_issues.title: "Apply" on python code not working
source_issues.evidence: User reports that in agent mode, Apply highlights code initially but the highlight disappears and the VSCode buffer is never updated when working on Python files. C++ works correctly.

source_issues.title: ALT+A快捷键APPLY CODE好像是有BUG,浪费了我大量的TOKENS
source_issues.evidence: ALT+A hotkey triggers Apply Code, conflicts with other VSCode plugins causing page to flicker for ~1 minute, no changes applied, user reports significant token waste.

signals.topic: Code autocomplete completely non-functional across multiple environments
signals.summary: The code autocomplete feature does not work at all — no suggestions are shown as users type. Affects multiple platforms (Windows, Linux code-server) and multiple model configurations (Ollama, Gemini). Core IDE productivity feature is unavailable.
signals.review_reason: Two users on different OSes and model configurations report autocomplete not functioning — one reports zero suggestions, the other reports severe performance degradation that makes VSCode unusable. Both are core IDE integration failures affecting the primary productivity feature. Count=2 with consistent symptom across environments.

source_issues.title: Autocomplete for code is not working
source_issues.evidence: User reports 'Code autocomplete isn't working; it simply does nothing. It doesn't show any code suggestions.' Tried disabling Copilot, small models, large models — nothing works. YouTube video provided showing zero suggestions appearing. Environment: Windows 11, Continue 1.2.22, Ollama qwen2.5-coder.

source_issues.title: Continue dev plugin: autocompletion is making VS-Code slow
source_issues.evidence: VS Code became very laggy when continue plugin is enabled. Saving (Ctrl+S) requires multiple attempts, copy-paste fails. Inline suggestions keep loading. Disabling the plugin restores normal performance. Environment: Ubuntu 20.04, Continue v1.0.5, Codestral model.

signals.topic: OpenAI adapter timeout config unit mismatch — seconds treated as milliseconds
signals.summary: The OpenAI adapter passes user-set timeout values directly to the OpenAI JS SDK without unit conversion. Users set timeout in seconds (e.g. 300 for 5 min) but the SDK expects milliseconds, resulting in 300ms timeout causing immediate 'Connection error' failures especially for local models.
aliases: connection error due to timeout misconfiguration
signals.review_reason: Root cause is clearly identified via code-level analysis. The bug is a silent failure mode: local models appear to fail with 'Connection error' when the real issue is a 2000x shorter timeout than intended. This is likely affecting multiple users (referenced as root cause for #11818). The issue identifies the exact file and line number. Confidence is very high.

source_issues.title: OpenAI adapter passes timeout to SDK without unit conversion (seconds vs milliseconds)
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis shows OpenAI.ts line 48 passes timeout directly to SDK without multiplying by 1000. A user setting timeout:300 gets a 300ms timeout instead of 300 seconds — 2000x shorter. Issue identifies this as likely root cause for #11818 and related connection error reports. Local models that need time to load are immediately failing.

signals.topic: Agent mode file editing tool overwrites files with model thought content or tool-call artifacts
signals.summary: In agent mode, when asking to edit files, the edit tool overwrites the file with the model's thinking output, tool call metadata, or suggestion prompts instead of actual code changes. The file gets corrupted with non-code content.
aliases: file content replaced with model thoughts
edit tool outputs wrong content to file
signals.review_reason: This is a data-corrupting bug — agent mode literally overwrites user files with model thinking content instead of code changes. Screenshots confirm the file content is corrupted. This is a critical destructive failure that users may not notice immediately. Very high severity even though only one report exists.

source_issues.title: File editing tool in agent mode overwrites the file with model thoughts not with actual changes
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'it seems it replaces the whole file with some output that is supposed to be in the chat.' Logs show the edit tool receives model thought content and tool call instructions instead of actual code changes. Screenshots confirm the file is corrupted with model output. Also reported with qwen3:14b model where thinking process is output in the edited file.

signals.topic: MCP SSE restarts break communication — Continue fails to re-establish session
signals.summary: When an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server using SSE restarts, Continue does not re-establish the session and attempts to continue with the old stale session, breaking communication entirely.
aliases: MCP session not re-established after restart
signals.review_reason: MCP is a key integration point for Continue. When MCP restarts (common in development), Continue silently fails to re-establish the session, breaking the entire MCP-dependent workflow. This is a recurring failure that requires manual intervention. Reported for SSE MCPs specifically.

source_issues.title: (sse) mcp restarts breaks communication
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'when the mcp is restarted continue is not re-establishing the session. I think it just wants to continue with the old session.' User explicitly requests that the code adapt to try and get a new session when communication fails.

signals.topic: cache_breakpoint flag causes crew execution failure for all non-Anthropic LLM providers (Groq, OpenAI-compatible)
signals.summary: mark_cache_breakpoint() is called unconditionally in agent_executor.py but strip_cache_breakpoint() is never invoked for non-Anthropic providers. Groq and OpenAI-compatible APIs reject the cache_breakpoint field, causing immediate crew failure with a BadRequestError. Users must apply a monkey-patch workaround to use any non-Anthropic provider.
aliases: non-Anthropic LLM provider rejection of cache_breakpoint field
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：任何使用Groq或OpenAI兼容端点的用户都无法运行crew，必须使用临时monkey-patch才能绕过。这是版本1.14.4引入的阻断性回归，直接影响所有非Anthropic LLM用户。

source_issues.title: [BUG] cache_breakpoint injected into messages for non-Anthropic providers (Groq, OpenAI-compatible)
source_issues.evidence: GroqException: 'messages.0': property 'cache_breakpoint' is unsupported. Crew fails immediately with BadRequestError. Full traceback provided. Workaround requires monkey-patching crewai.llms.cache.

signals.topic: Task retry has no idempotency guard — duplicate payments, emails, and trades on retry
signals.summary: When a task fails and retries via max_retry_limit or external re-trigger, any @tool that already executed runs again with no deduplication mechanism. In-memory dedup doesn't survive worker re-dispatch. This causes duplicate side effects in production: duplicate charges, duplicate emails, duplicate trades.
aliases: tool re-execution on retry causes duplicate side effects
no idempotency guard for tool calls on task retry
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用/成本损失风险：生产环境中使用@tool执行支付、邮件、交易等副作用操作时，任务重试会导致重复执行，直接造成财务损失。社区36条评论证实生产影响，同等问题在LangGraph Cloud独立出现，修复需框架层面提供幂等保障。

source_issues.title: Tool re-execution on task retry has no idempotency guard — duplicate payments, emails, trades possible
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows @tool with Stripe charge that fires twice on retry. 36 comments from community confirming production impact. LangGraph Cloud issue #7417 documents same failure mode independently. Fix requires durable external storage, not in-memory dedup.

signals.topic: LLM model name prefix filter too strict — custom/self-hosted model deployments excluded
signals.summary: crewAI's llm.py filters models by prefix ['claude-', 'anthropic.'] only. Users with self-deployed models using different naming conventions (e.g., 'anthropic--claude-...') are filtered out, leading to incorrect output behavior. No support for custom model naming prefixes.
aliases: custom model naming prefix not supported
self-hosted model filtered out by prefix matching
signals.review_reason: 明显体验下降：使用自定义部署模型的用户无法正常使用crewAI，因为模型名称不符合严格的['claude-', 'anthropic.']前缀规则，导致输出行为不正确。这是v1.14.2引入的回归，影响所有自定义模型部署场景。

source_issues.title: [BUG] Model naming prefixes filtering is too strict
source_issues.evidence: User has self-deployed Anthropic-compatible model with naming 'anthropic--claude-...' which is filtered out by strict prefix matching, leading to incorrect behavior. Specific code location provided (llm.py L469).

signals.topic: DeepSeek-V4 thinking mode returns reasoning_content not handled by crewAI — LLM calls fail
signals.summary: DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Pro return both 'content' and 'reasoning_content' in thinking mode. crewAI does not handle the reasoning_content parameter, causing API call failures with 400 invalid_request_error when used as the LLM provider.
aliases: thinking mode response handling missing for DeepSeek
signals.review_reason: 关键LLM不可用：使用DeepSeek-V4-Flash或Pro模型时thinking模式返回的reasoning_content参数未被处理，导致LLM调用返回400错误，crew完全无法执行。这是最新DeepSeek模型的兼容性问题，影响主流用户。

source_issues.title: [FEATURE]The latest version of DeepSeek is incompatible with reasoning_content.
source_issues.evidence: LLM call fails with 400 error: 'reasoning_content in thinking mode must be passed back to the API'. Flow execution error logged. User explicitly identifying as a bug with full error traceback provided.

signals.topic: Dependency version conflict between crewAI and OpenLIT blocks installation
signals.summary: crewAI 1.14.4 pins opentelemetry-sdk to exactly 1.35.0, but OpenLIT 1.41.2+ requires opentelemetry-sdk >=1.38.0. This causes poetry lock and pip install failures when both dependencies are used together, blocking project setup.
aliases: opentelemetry-sdk version conflict blocks OpenLIT integration
poetry lock fails due to opentelemetry version mismatch
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：依赖版本冲突导致poetry lock失败，用户无法同时使用crewAI和OpenLIT进行可观测性监控。这阻止了完整的项目初始化，在需要可观测性的生产环境中是明确的阻断项。

source_issues.title: [BUG] dependency conflict with OpenLIT
source_issues.evidence: poetry lock fails with dependency conflict error when both crewai 1.14.4 and openlit 1.42.0 are specified. 2 comments confirming issue. Windows 11 + Python 3.10 + Poetry environment confirmed.

signals.topic: Antigravity CLI migration breaks paying users: AVX incompatibility, unusable rate limits, and forced Google One subscription disruption
signals.summary: Users are being forced to migrate from the stable Node.js Gemini CLI to the Go-based Antigravity CLI, which breaks on legacy CPUs lacking AVX instructions, enforces new rate limits users describe as unusable, and disrupts Google One subscription access for paid users.
aliases: Google One subscription unusable after migration
AVX instruction set requirement blocks legacy CPUs
signals.review_reason: This is a multi-faceted migration disaster for paying customers. Three independent reports with 8+ community comments collectively document: (1) legacy CPU users completely blocked by AVX requirement, (2) rate limits described as 'unusable' for paying subscribers, and (3) OAuth stability broken after migration. June 18 forced cutoff deadline creates time pressure. This blocks the primary use case (CLI access) for paid Google One AI Pro subscribers, meeting P0 criteria.

source_issues.title: Compatibility Issue: Antigravity CLI requires AVX instructions missing on legacy CPUs (AMD A-Series)

source_issues.title: Keep google one for gemini cli

OAuth workflow becomes 'extremely unstable' with 429 Resource Exhausted or session lockouts after just 2-3 multi-turn prompts. signals.topic: WSL/Windows shell execution hangs, drops output, or freezes terminal when running Windows executables
signals.summary: Gemini CLI hangs, loses/drops output, or freezes the terminal when executing Windows .exe binaries (adb, git, etc.) on WSL, due to Linux PTY (node-pty) incompatibility with Windows binaries. Also affects embedded terminal on Windows after subprocess commands.

source_issues.evidence: Windows binaries (.exe) inside Gemini CLI on WSL hang, lose output, or fail to terminate cleanly. Fix suggested: detect WSL+exe and bypass node-pty.

source_issues.title: Embedded Gemini CLI Terminal Freezes/Glitches After Background Process Commands on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Terminal on Windows enters stuck 'Thinking...' state after executing shell commands like taskkill. UI shows background processes but terminal input/output becomes unresponsive. subprocess cleanup desynchronized.

signals.topic: ENOTDIR Unhandled Promise Rejection crashes CLI when parsing multi-line prompts

The CLI incorrectly attempts to treat prompt text as a file path during a permission check, causing a crash that blocks the entire session.
aliases: CLI crashes when pasting multi-line instructions

Two identical reports from the same user confirm the reproducibility. While marked as possible duplicate, the bug is real and blocking.

source_issues.title: ENOTDIR Unhandled Promise Rejection when parsing multi-line prompt
source_issues.evidence: CLI crashes with ENOTDIR: not a directory, lstat. Stack trace: robustRealpath -> resolveToRealPath -> checkPermissions. Triggered when pasting multi-line instructions containing paths or quotes. Error: unhandled promise rejection.

source_issues.title: ENOTDIR Unhandled Promise Rejection when parsing multi-line prompt
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of 27338. Same error: ENOTDIR crash when pasting multi-line prompt containing path-like strings.

signals.topic: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED on cloudcode-pa endpoint blocks Google One AI Pro subscribers from using the CLI
signals.summary: Google One AI Pro subscribers with valid OAuth sign-in get 403 PERMISSION_DENIED errors on every prompt because the CLI sends requests to cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com with a phantom project ID from a ghost project. Two community fixes (PR #25450, PR #26420) exist but were never merged, leaving users blocked for an extended period.
aliases: phantom project ID causes auth failure
signals.review_reason: Although count=1, the author explicitly references 35+ prior identical issues. The root cause is well-identified (phantom project + GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT override) and two reviewed PRs confirm fix feasibility. This is a sustained auth regression for paying subscribers that makes the CLI completely unusable for every prompt. The review_reason gives explicit evidence of widespread user impact.

source_issues.title: " Error 403 " on cloudcode-pa still happening — checked main branch, two proposed fixes (#25450, #26420) were never merged, users still blocked!!
source_issues.evidence: Google One AI Pro subscriber with valid OAuth gets 403 on every prompt at cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com. Author identifies 35+ prior issues with the same pattern. Root cause: loadCodeAssist returns a phantom cloudaicompanionProject for personal accounts; CodeAssistServer uses it without stripping. Also: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT env var forces enterprise path for OAuth users. Two ready-to-merge PRs exist (#25450, #26420) for weeks with no action.

signals.topic: /copy command fails on Windows with clipboard fallback binary not found

The fallback binary is missing from the bundled environment, leaving users with no workaround. While single report, the failure mode is complete and reproducible across terminal types.

source_issues.title: /copy doesn't work in Windows VS Code

Reproduced on Windows 11, VS Code Insiders, PowerShell 7.6.1, and Git Bash. No workaround found. /copy is a core usability feature.

signals.topic: LocalPythonExecutor沙箱可通过ctypes模块逃逸，执行任意系统命令
