signals.review_reason: 关键安全漏洞：ctypes不在DANGEROUS_MODULES黑名单中，导致LocalPythonExecutor沙箱形同虚设，任意代码可逃逸并执行系统命令，属于严重安全缺陷且有明确代码位置（local_python_executor.py L130-L141）。

source_issues.title: [Security] Sandbox escape via ctypes in LocalPythonExecutor
source_issues.evidence: LocalPythonExecutor的DANGEROUS_MODULES列表缺少ctypes模块，恶意代码可通过ctypes调用libc.system()在宿主机执行任意命令，直接绕过所有沙箱限制。已有huntr.com漏洞赏金报告。

signals.topic: deepagents deploy silently drops MCP tools when mcp.json headers contain unresolved ${VAR} references
signals.summary: During `deepagents deploy`, environment variable references like `${API_KEY}` in mcp.json headers are not expanded before being forwarded to MultiServerMCPClient. The unresolved literal string causes an HTTP 401 auth failure, which is then swallowed by a bare `try/except: return []` in `_load_mcp_tools()`. The agent boots successfully but sees zero MCP tools with no visible error — a silent, complete failure of MCP tool exposure.
aliases: mcp.json env var expansion missing in deploy
MCP tools silently fail to load on deployment due to unresolved headers
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed reports with explicit user impact evidence: MCP tools are silently dropped during deployment with no error shown. The agent boots successfully, making the failure invisible to users who expect their MCP servers to be available. This is a complete functional loss for MCP-dependent workflows, not a minor degradation.

source_issues.title: `deepagents deploy` does not expand `${VAR}` references in `mcp.json` header values
source_issues.evidence: Config works with `dcode` but silently breaks when shipped through `deepagents deploy`. MCP server returns 401 due to literal `${VAR}` in header. `_load_mcp_tools()` exception swallowed, agent sees zero tools with no visible error.

source_issues.title: deepagents deploy: `${VAR}` references in `mcp.json` headers are not expanded
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #3508. `MCP_TOOLS_TEMPLATE` in `libs/cli/deepagents_cli/deploy/templates.py` forwards headers verbatim without `os.path.expandvars`. Confirmed 401 + silent tool disappearance.

signals.topic: BaseSandbox.grep() crashes with ValueError when file paths contain colons
signals.summary: SandboxBackend.grep() uses `grep -rHnF` and parses output with `line.split(':', 2)`, assuming format `path:line_number:text`. File paths containing colons (e.g. timestamps like `device_20260519:0606_syslog.log`) cause the split to misalign, making `int(parts[1])` receive a non-numeric string and raise ValueError, crashing the agent loop.
aliases: grep crash on colon in filename
ValueError in grep when path contains colon separator
signals.review_reason: Confirmed crash with stack trace and reproducer. While count=1, the crash propagates out of the agent loop and terminates the run — a workflow-blocking failure for any user with colons in their file paths (common with timestamped or locale-formatted filenames). This is not an edge case in many development environments.

source_issues.title: BaseSandbox.grep() crashes with ValueError when file paths contain colons
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '30'` when grepping files with colon-delimited paths. Confirmed on v0.5.1 and v0.6.2. Stack trace shows crash in `sandbox.py` line 688. Suggestion to use `ripgrep --json` for structured output.

signals.topic: SandboxBackend.grep() crashes with ValueError when container exec fails (OCI runtime error parsed as grep output)
signals.summary: SandboxBackend.grep() crashes with ValueError when the underlying container exec fails at the OCI runtime layer (e.g. invalid work_dir). The OCI runtime's error message contains colons (e.g. 'OCI runtime exec failed: exec failed:...'), passes the `len(parts) >= 3` guard, and then crashes on `int(parts[1])`. The agent loop terminates instead of returning a graceful error.
aliases: grep crash on container exec failure
OCI runtime error message parsed as grep output causing crash
signals.review_reason: Confirmed crash with complete stack trace and Docker-based reproducer. The crash terminates the agent run rather than gracefully surfacing an error. This is a workflow-blocking failure that could occur in any sandbox environment with misconfigured paths or runtime issues.

source_issues.title: SandboxBackend.grep crashes with `ValueError` when container exec fails
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace: `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ' exec failed'`. Root cause: OCI runtime error stdout contains colons, passes split guard, then `int()` on non-digit fails. Expected: `GrepResult(error=..., matches=None)`. Actual: ValueError terminates agent run. Environment: deepagents 0.6.1, Docker on Linux.

signals.topic: DeepAgents agent.invoke is ~50x slower than raw Langchain (~349s vs ~10s for equivalent workload)
signals.summary: A user reports that `deepagents` `agent.invoke` takes ~349 seconds for a task that takes ~6s with raw OpenAI API and ~10s with Langchain alone. The overhead is attributed to deepagents internals, not the LLM or tools. The user is blocked from using deepagents for deep research workloads.
signals.review_reason: Single confirmed report with quantitative benchmarks showing ~50x slowdown vs Langchain baseline. The user is actively blocked from using the product for their stated use case (deep research agent). While count=1, the severity and specificity of the performance numbers (detailed timing breakdown) make this credible user-impact evidence. The tool-only overhead is ruled out by the user.

source_issues.title: Slow response with agent.invoke
source_issues.evidence: Benchmark: OpenAI direct 6.3s, Langchain 10.1s, DeepAgents 349.3s. Individual LLM call within DeepAgents takes 566.9s. Reproducer provided with `create_deep_agent`. User blocked from using deepagents for deep research. deepagents 0.6.1, Python 3.12.3.

signals.topic: ChatAnthropic.bind_tools mutates caller-provided tool_choice dict, causing unexpected state leakage across multi-turn calls
signals.summary: When ChatAnthropic.bind_tools receives tool_choice as a dict, it stores and mutates the original object in place (adding disable_parallel_tool_use). Reusing the same dict across calls causes silent option leakage.
signals.review_reason: Non-obvious state leakage: the caller-provided dict is silently mutated with no error or warning. Agents that reuse tool_choice across multiple invocations get unexpected parallel_tool_calls behavior. This breaks multi-turn conversation flows where the same model instance serves different tool configurations. Count=2 confirms it's a pattern, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: ChatAnthropic.bind_tools mutates caller-provided tool_choice dict
source_issues.evidence: When parallel_tool_calls is set, ChatAnthropic.bind_tools stores the caller-provided dict directly and adds disable_parallel_tool_use to it in place. If the same dict is reused across calls, the option silently leaks into later calls, breaking multi-turn agent behavior with no error.

source_issues.title: ChatAnthropic.bind_tools mutates caller-provided tool_choice dict
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed duplicate of #37596 — same in-place dict mutation root cause.

signals.topic: Anthropic base64 file blocks reject non-PDF mime types, blocking CSV/TXT/MD file processing pipelines
signals.summary: Sending standard type:'file' content blocks with mime_type 'text/csv' (and other text types) to ChatAnthropic fails because mime_type is forwarded verbatim, but Anthropic API only accepts 'application/pdf'.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for document processing pipelines: users cannot send common file types (CSV, TXT, MD, DOCX, XLSX) to Anthropic even though the API supports them as text. The library incorrectly restricts to PDF only, completely breaking RAG use cases on non-PDF documents.

source_issues.title: anthropic: base64 file blocks with non-PDF text mime types fail with media_type validation error
source_issues.evidence: mime_type='text/csv' forwarded verbatim to Anthropic API which only accepts 'application/pdf'. Error: 'messages.0.content.1.document.source.base64.media_type: Input should be application/pdf'. This blocks all text-based file RAG pipelines (CSV, TXT, MD, DOCX, XLSX).

source_issues.title: anthropic: base64 file blocks with non-PDF text mime types fail with media_type validation error
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed duplicate of #37576.

signals.topic: ChatOpenRouter creates new httpx clients per instantiation with no caching, causing TLS connection leaks in production factory patterns
signals.summary: Every ChatOpenRouter instance creates a new httpx.Client/AsyncClient with no default-client caching. In LangGraph factory graphs and FastAPI dependency injection, this causes TLS connection leaks and hits resource limits.
signals.review_reason: Significant production degradation: each request creates unreclaimed TLS connections. In LangGraph factory patterns and FastAPI DI (documented and common usage patterns), this exhausts connection resources before model rate limits are hit. The same root cause was previously fixed for AzureChatOpenAI, confirming the anti-pattern. Causes resource exhaustion crashes in production.

source_issues.title: langchain-openrouter: ChatOpenRouter creates fresh httpx clients per instantiation (no default-client caching)
source_issues.evidence: Every ChatOpenRouter instance creates new httpx.Client/AsyncClient with no caching. In LangGraph factory graphs and FastAPI dependency injection, TLS connections leak and resource limits are hit. Same issue was previously fixed for AzureChatOpenAI in PR #32531, confirming the pattern.

source_issues.title: langchain-openrouter: ChatOpenRouter creates fresh httpx clients per instantiation (no default-client caching)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed duplicate of #37498.

signals.topic: tool_search_tool_result streaming index field not stripped, breaking multi-turn agent conversations after first tool use
signals.summary: The index field from streaming chunk assembly is not stripped before the assembled AIMessage enters conversation history. The next API call fails with HTTP 400 'Extra inputs are not permitted'.
signals.review_reason: Complete main flow failure for agents using tool_search with streaming: after the first turn, every subsequent API call fails with HTTP 400 due to invalid index field in conversation history. The agent becomes completely non-functional. Clear, specific user impact with exact error message.

source_issues.title: BUG: tool_search_tool_result blocks retain stream-chunk index field, breaking multi-turn API calls
source_issues.evidence: index field from streaming chunk assembly is not stripped before the assembled AIMessage is stored in conversation history. Next API call fails: HTTP 400 'messages.N.content.M.tool_search_tool_result.index: Extra inputs are not permitted'. Agent completely breaks after first tool use.

signals.topic: Agent.save()/Chain.save() writes files without explicit UTF-8 encoding, failing on Windows and non-UTF-8 locales
signals.summary: Path.open('w') without explicit encoding falls back to locale-dependent encoding (cp1252 on Windows). Agents saved on Linux cannot be loaded on Windows, causing UnicodeDecodeError for prompts and tool docstrings with non-ASCII characters.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure on cross-platform workflows: agents saved on Linux cannot be loaded on Windows (common in enterprise environments). Users in Windows environments are completely blocked from loading agents created on Linux. Specific error evidence with clear platform scope.

source_issues.title: Agent.save() and Chain.save() write JSON/YAML without explicit encoding='utf-8' — fails on Windows / non-utf-8 locales
source_issues.evidence: Path.open('w') without encoding falls back to locale.getpreferredencoding() which is cp1252 on Windows. UnicodeDecodeError when loading agents saved on Linux. Prompts, descriptions, and tool docstrings routinely contain non-ASCII characters.

signals.topic: InMemoryStore.search() crashes when filtered items have missing keys or non-numeric values
signals.summary: InMemoryStore.search() with $gt/$gte/$lt/$lte filters raises unhandled TypeError/ValueError when any item in the namespace is missing the filtered key or has a non-numeric value, poisoning the entire search instead of excluding the item.
aliases: InMemoryStore search crash on null/missing fields
signals.review_reason: Runtime crash of a core API (InMemoryStore.search) triggered by legitimate data in production use (mixed-type schemas). Contradicts documented PostgreSQL-compatible behavior and breaks the core search contract. Single-issue P1 due to count<3.

source_issues.title: InMemoryStore.search() crashes on $gt/$gte/$lt/$lte when an item is missing the filtered key or has a non-numeric value
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'NoneType' — any item missing the filtered key or storing a non-numeric value causes the entire search to abort rather than being excluded from results.

signals.topic: Thread copy endpoint is synchronous and blocking — can take 12+ minutes causing serverless timeouts
signals.summary: The thread copy endpoint is synchronous with no async/progress/shallow-copy option, observed taking over 12 minutes on large conversations, causing AWS Lambda 15-minute hard timeouts and leaving the application in an uncertain state.
aliases: thread copy endpoint synchronous blocking timeout
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: users cannot fork/duplicate conversations in production serverless deployments due to AWS Lambda hard timeout. The 'fork chat' feature is completely broken for real workloads. Single-issue P1 due to severe production impact outweighing frequency.

source_issues.title: Thread copy endpoint can take 12+ minutes with no async/progress or shallow-copy option
source_issues.evidence: Thread copy observed taking 12+ minutes; synchronous endpoint with no async/progress/shallow-copy option; AWS Lambda 15-minute hard timeout hit, leaving app in uncertain state; 'fork chat' feature unusable in production serverless environments.

signals.topic: SDK HTTP client reuses stale Content-Length/Content-Type headers on reconnect, causing protocol errors
signals.summary: HttpClient.request_reconnect reuses Content-Length and Content-Type headers from the original POST body on a body-less GET reconnect, causing h11.LocalProtocolError that silently prevents runs.wait() and runs.cancel(wait=True) from succeeding.
signals.review_reason: Core SDK operations (wait for run completion, cancel run) silently fail with a protocol error on reconnect — users get no result and no error feedback on operations they depend on for orchestration. High-severity workflow failure despite single-issue count.

source_issues.title: langgraph_sdk: HttpClient.request_reconnect reuses Content-Length/Content-Type on body-less GET retry, causing h11.LocalProtocolError
source_issues.evidence: GET reconnect sent with Content-Length: 13 from original POST body while body is empty; LocalProtocolError: Too little data for declared Content-Length; affects client.runs.wait() and client.runs.cancel(wait=True); triggered by Location header + httpx.HTTPError on first attempt.

signals.topic: AsyncSqliteSaver.put() and put_writes() deadlock when called synchronously from within the event loop
signals.summary: AsyncSqliteSaver.put() and put_writes() lack the InvalidStateError guard present in other sync-bridge methods, causing the event loop to deadlock silently with no diagnostic when called synchronously from within the same loop.
aliases: asyncio deadlock in SQLite checkpoint saver
signals.review_reason: Application-level deadlock — the process hangs indefinitely with no error, making it nearly impossible to diagnose. Two sync-bridge methods are missing protection that the other four have, indicating a clear oversight. Single-issue P1 due to deadlock severity.

source_issues.title: AsyncSqliteSaver.put() and put_writes() deadlock instead of raising when called synchronously from within the event loop
source_issues.evidence: Sync bridge methods use asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result() which deadlocks when called from within the saver's own event loop; put and put_writes lack the guard that other methods have (get_tuple, list, delete_thread, get_delta_channel_history) that raises asyncio.InvalidStateError; deadlock produces no diagnostic.

signals.topic: SQLite checkpointer stores full checkpoint blobs without deduplication, causing database bloat exceeding 100 GiB
signals.summary: checkpoint-sqlite stores full serialized checkpoint blobs inline without using new_versions normalization like Postgres saver does, causing database to grow to 100+ GiB in long-running usage where only a subset of channels changed.
signals.review_reason: Production infrastructure cost issue: 100+ GiB database growth from a design flaw in the SQLite checkpointer causes disk exhaustion and degraded performance in long-running deployments. Clear cost-loss and infrastructure-impacting bug.

source_issues.title: checkpoint-sqlite: storage model does not use new_versions to normalize channel values like Postgres saver
source_issues.evidence: Downstream observed checkpoint database growth above 100 GiB in long-running usage; SQLite stores full serialized checkpoint inline while Postgres normalizes into checkpoint_blobs keyed by (thread_id, checkpoint_ns, channel, version); unchanged large channel values are serialized inline repeatedly; each of two checkpoint rows contains a 10,000,157 byte blob for the same unchanged value.

signals.topic: Suggested-questions feature fails with Pydantic ValidationError on AppModelConfigDict, causing 500 internal server error
signals.summary: Key feature completely broken — enabling suggested questions causes Pydantic ValidationError with missing required fields (annotation_reply, more_like_this, sensitive_word_avoidance.config, agent_mode.prompt). Affects v1.14.2 self-hosted deployments.
signals.review_reason: Key feature entirely broken. Enabling suggested questions triggers 500 errors and blocks the feature completely. Same regression reported independently twice — indicates incomplete fix. Affects active self-hosted v1.14.2 deployments, a core agent feature.

source_issues.title: suggested-questions always fails
source_issues.evidence: Pydantic ValidationError: 2 validation errors for AppModelConfigDict (annotation_reply and more_like_this Field required). Internal server error 500 on /console/api/apps/{id}/chat-messages/{id}/suggested-questions. v1.14.2 self-hosted Docker.

source_issues.title: suggested-questions failed
source_issues.evidence: Pydantic ValidationError: 4 validation errors (annotation_reply, more_like_this, sensitive_word_avoidance.config, agent_mode.prompt all required). Internal server error 500. v1.14.2 self-hosted Docker.

signals.topic: Sandbox code execution fails with 'no space left on device' storage error on Dify Cloud
signals.summary: Sandbox storage exhaustion blocks all code execution, returning -500 error when attempting to run sandbox-based workflows.
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks code execution feature — a core Dify capability — returning -500 error. Users cannot run any sandbox-based workflows, causing immediate feature unavailability on Dify Cloud.

source_issues.title: sandbox no space left on device
source_issues.evidence: Error code -500: 'open /var/sandbox/sandbox-python/tmp/{uuid}.py: no space left on device'. Dify Cloud, latest version. Sandbox code execution completely blocked.

signals.topic: Workflow loop node continues execution after exit condition is met, ignoring break logic
signals.summary: Loop node in workflow does not respect exit condition. When item 'a' requests loop exit, subsequent items 'b' and 'c' still execute, causing incorrect business logic and potential infinite loops.
signals.review_reason: Core workflow logic completely broken — loop exit condition is ignored, causing all iterations to execute regardless of break. Can cause infinite loops, wasted compute resources, and wrong business outcomes in production workflows. A fundamental workflow feature malfunction.

source_issues.title: Looping node, unable to exit the loop
source_issues.evidence: Loop=['a','b','c']. User sets 'a' to exit loop. Expected: only 'a' executes. Actual: 'a'->'b'->'c' all execute regardless of break. v1.11.2 self-hosted Docker.

signals.topic: Custom tool shows as 'Tool removed' after agent publish and page refresh
signals.summary: After publishing an agent with a custom tool and refreshing the page, the tool displays as 'Tool removed' and becomes unusable, breaking agent functionality.
signals.review_reason: Breaks the standard publish-and-use workflow for agents with custom tools. After a routine publish+refresh cycle, tools silently disappear and agents malfunction. Users cannot reliably deploy custom tool-based agents in production.

source_issues.title: Tool removed
source_issues.evidence: Steps: create custom tool, add to agent, publish agent, refresh page. Result: tool shows 'Tool removed' and becomes non-functional. v1.11.4 self-hosted Docker. Blocks production agent deployments.

signals.topic: Local plugin triggers marketplace HTTP requests when marketplace is disabled, causing spurious 500 errors

aliases: agent node click triggers external API
signals.review_reason: Configuration is silently bypassed — air-gapped or offline deployments still make external HTTP calls. Generates confusing 500 error messages in the UI for users who explicitly disabled marketplace, degrading trust in configuration controls.

source_issues.title: Tool plugins inside agent nodes send HTTP request to dify marketplace when the node is clicked and Marketplace is turned off
source_issues.evidence: MARKETPLACE_ENABLED=false but clicking agent node with local plugin still sends HTTP to marketplace API, returning 500. Causes spurious error message in UI. v1.14.1 self-hosted Docker.

signals.topic: 记忆重复存储且无时间维度加权，偏好随时间冲突时结果随机
signals.summary: 用户重复表达偏好时，记忆被重复存储而非合并。召回时相似内容未根据时间维度加权，导致偏好随时间发生冲突时（如先说喜欢可乐→再说喜欢咖啡→最后又说喜欢可乐），最终召回结果随机，无法反映用户最新偏好。核心记忆管理语义失效。
aliases: similar memories not deduplicated, no time-based weighting
outdated memories not overwritten, preference conflicts not resolved
signals.review_reason: 记忆管理核心语义失效：重复偏好无法去重 + 旧记忆不自动过期，导致 AI 基于冲突/过时记忆给出随机响应。虽非崩溃性阻断，但直接影响 AI 辅助决策质量，两个独立 issue 从不同角度反映了同一根本缺陷。

source_issues.title: similar memories repeat quite frequently
source_issues.evidence: 用户重复表达偏好时记忆重复存储；相似内容召回时无时间加权；前脚说喜欢可乐→后脚说喜欢咖啡→又说喜欢可乐，召回结果随机，偏好发生错乱。

source_issues.title: Automatically overwrite the out-of-date memory
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确表示旧记忆应被新记忆覆盖，但当前系统两条记忆均被存储，search 查询时两者以相近分数返回，无法区分哪个是最新的。

source_issues.evidence: 同一问题的重复提交（已 closed），同一根因：Framer CMS 组件中 FAQ 文字颜色 token 使用了错误值 #020202 而非 #ffffff。

signals.topic: xai provider 工厂构造即崩溃，tools 参数静默丢失，tool_call 响应未解析

xai LLM provider crashes on any factory use
