signals.topic: LiteLLM custom header (X-Application-Name) configuration not applied, blocking API calls to header-required servers
signals.summary: Aider does not forward user-configured custom HTTP headers to LiteLLM, causing API calls to fail with 400 errors on LiteLLM proxy servers that require the X-Application-Name header.
signals.review_reason: #5160 blocks the primary workflow: the user cannot use aider with their LiteLLM server at all because API calls fail with 400. The user's attempt to configure extra_headers is ineffective, indicating a missing feature or bug in how aider passes headers to litellm. This is a key functional breakdown for the affected user.

source_issues.title: X-Application-Name Header requested from an LiteLLM Server
source_issues.evidence: litellm.APIError: OpenAIException - {'message':'X-Application-Name header is missing (status_code=400)}' — user tried extra_headers in model config with no effect; API calls to LiteLLM server are completely blocked

signals.topic: Filtered named metric aggregation produces incorrect totals/averages for legacy/imported rows without stored namedScoreWeights
signals.summary: When a result row has multiple component assertions contributing to the same named metric and no stored `gradingResult.namedScoreWeights`, the filtered SQL path falls back to one row/weight per result, producing a smaller `namedScoresCount` and `namedScoreWeights` than the canonical prompt metrics path. This causes the UI to display incorrect totals and averages for named metrics on legacy or imported data.
signals.review_reason: Data accuracy defect causing incorrect metric reporting in the UI. Users relying on named metric averages in filtered views will see wrong totals. The mismatch between filtered and canonical metrics is a non-trivial data correctness issue that can mislead evaluation decisions.

source_issues.title: Align filtered named metric denominators with prompt metrics
source_issues.evidence: The UI prefers namedScoreWeights as denominator; filtered named metric totals/averages disagree with canonical prompt metrics for legacy/imported rows. Root cause: optimized filtered SQL path falls back to one row/weight per result instead of counting component assertions.

signals.topic: Named metric chart renders NaN when all prompt values for a metric are zero
signals.summary: Named metric chart data normalization divides each prompt value by the maximum value for that metric. When every prompt has 0 for a named metric, the maximum is also 0, resulting in 0/0 = NaN being sent to the chart renderer, causing non-finite chart data.
signals.review_reason: Direct UI rendering failure. Charts with NaN values are broken visualizations that prevent users from reading evaluation data. This is a visible, clearly incorrect output that makes a core evaluation feature unusable whenever all prompts score zero on a named metric.

source_issues.title: Avoid NaN values in named metric charts
source_issues.evidence: Chart normalization produces 0/0 when all named metric values are zero, generating NaN instead of finite chart data. All-zero metrics (e.g. unused or zero-scoring named metrics) render broken charts.

signals.topic: Eval result count cache returns stale data for up to 5 minutes after new results are written
signals.summary: getCachedResultsCount() and getTotalResultRowCount() cache result counts per eval with a 5-minute TTL. The result write paths (EvalResult.createFromEvaluateResult, EvalResult.createManyFromEvaluateResult) do not invalidate these caches after inserting rows. Users who create an eval, check results before the cache expires, then insert results will see a stale zero count until TTL expires.
aliases: cache invalidation missing after result insert
signals.review_reason: Data consistency bug causing users to see incorrect (stale zero) result counts in the UI for up to 5 minutes after inserting results. This directly disrupts the core eval workflow where users need accurate counts to confirm their results were written successfully.

source_issues.title: Invalidate eval result count caches after result writes
source_issues.evidence: Cache TTL is 5 minutes. Result write paths do not call clearCountCache(). Concrete scenario: create eval with no results, cache count=0, insert rows, query count again before TTL expiry — stored rows are correct but count consumers see stale 0.

signals.topic: Manual rating edits cause prompt-level aggregate metrics (pass/fail/score) to drift out of sync
signals.summary: The manual rating update route modifies a result row's success, score, and gradingResult but does not apply corresponding deltas to the prompt-level aggregate metrics. Prompt metrics are derived by summing stored result rows, so after a manual rating update the aggregate counts can disagree with the individual rows.
aliases: prompt aggregate metrics out of sync after edit
signals.review_reason: Data integrity violation after manual rating edits: prompt-level pass/fail counts, scores, and assertion statistics become inconsistent with the underlying result rows. Users trusting aggregate metrics after making manual edits will see incorrect evaluation summaries.

source_issues.title: Keep manual rating aggregate metrics in sync
source_issues.evidence: Rating route updates row-level fields but not prompt aggregates. Concrete drift cases: same-pass score change, same-fail score change, existing manual rating score change, clearing a manual rating. Prompt-level pass/fail/error counts and assertion counts become incorrect.

signals.topic: Eval table API endpoint has no upper bound on page size for non-export requests, risking server resource exhaustion
signals.summary: GET /api/eval/:id/table accepts any positive integer for limit on normal table requests. Unlike export requests which use Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, non-export page requests have no upper bound. A large limit value forces the server to load and serialize a large amount of eval result data in a single response.
aliases: missing limit cap on eval table API
signals.review_reason: Missing resource boundary on a server API endpoint. While no active exploitation is reported, the lack of a limit cap allows clients to trigger excessive server-side memory usage, which can degrade or crash the service for other users. This is a defensive hardening issue with potential DoS impact, assigned P2 as no active user impact has been documented.

source_issues.title: Cap eval table page size for non-export requests
source_issues.evidence: No upper bound on limit parameter for non-export GET /api/eval/:id/table requests. Server loads and serializes all matching rows in one response. Other list-style APIs in the server already bound page sizes — this endpoint deviates from established resource-control pattern.

signals.topic: Ollama streaming QueryEngine yields entire answer as single chunk instead of incremental tokens
signals.summary: When using `query_engine.query()` with `streaming=True` on Ollama Qwen2.5, `response.response_gen` only yields one complete chunk containing the full answer instead of streaming incremental tokens. This breaks progressive UI rendering in real-time RAG applications where users expect to see answers appear token-by-token.
aliases: QueryEngine streaming yields full response at once
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug that blocks the core streaming workflow for RAG applications. When streaming=True on the QueryEngine, users expect progressive token-level output for real-time UI updates. Instead, the entire answer is returned as a single chunk, defeating the entire purpose of streaming. While count=1, the impact is severe (core feature completely non-functional for Ollama) and the user has no viable workaround within the query engine API.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: StreamingResponse.response_gen only yields one complete chunk when using Ollama Qwen2.5 with QueryEngine streaming
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly demonstrates that `response.response_gen` yields only one chunk containing the entire final answer instead of incremental tokens. The user is blocked from building a progressive streaming frontend for their RAG application using Ollama. Workaround of bypassing `query_engine.query()` is mentioned but not acceptable.

signals.topic: WeaviateVectorStore fails to import due to breaking change in weaviate-client v4.20.5
signals.summary: Upgrading weaviate-client to v4.20.5 causes an ImportError when importing WeaviateVectorStore from llama_index, because the library imports an internal class `_ContextManagerWrapper` that no longer exists in the new client version. Users are blocked from using the Weaviate vector store integration after a routine dependency upgrade.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed startup crash triggered by a breaking change in a downstream dependency (weaviate-client v4.20.5). The WeaviateVectorStore fails to import entirely, making the integration completely unusable. Users performing routine dependency upgrades are immediately blocked. While count=1, the impact is a complete import failure of a first-party integration package, which qualifies as a P1 user pain point.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ImportError: cannot import name '_ContextManagerWrapper' with weaviate-client v4.20.5
source_issues.evidence: User reports ImportError on upgrade to weaviate-client==4.20.5 when importing WeaviateVectorStore. The error occurs at `llama_index/vector_stores/weaviate/base.py:39` attempting to import `_ContextManagerWrapper` from `weaviate.collections.batch.batch_wrapper`, which no longer exists. This is a blocking import failure that prevents the entire Weaviate integration from loading.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock integration hardcodes model list, blocking access to newer models (Qwen, OpenAI OSS-120) without using LangChain
signals.summary: AWS Bedrock LLM integration in LlamaIndex has a hardcoded list of supported models. Users trying to use newer Bedrock models like `openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0` (Qwen) or `openai-oss-120` encounter failures because the models are not in the allowlist. The user reports being forced to abandon LlamaIndex and switch to LangChain mid-project due to this limitation.
aliases: AWS Bedrock new model support missing
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed blocking issue where a hardcoded model allowlist in the Bedrock LLM integration prevents users from accessing newer AWS Bedrock models. The user explicitly reports being forced to abandon LlamaIndex mid-project and switch to LangChain — a concrete, costly user impact. While count=1, the pattern of hardcoded model lists is a systemic issue that blocks any user wanting to use newer Bedrock model variants.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Bedrok Model Not Support - Qween, openai-oss-120
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'now in the middle of my project I suddenly know that llamaindex has hard coded settings for these models. I have to move to langhcain. just leave the llmaindex for llm call.' This is a concrete case of a user being forced to abandon LlamaIndex mid-project due to hardcoded model restrictions in the Bedrock LLM integration.

signals.topic: download_loader removed from llama_index public API, breaking third-party integrations including Haystack-LlamaHub connector
signals.summary: The `download_loader` function was removed from the `llama_index` public API without a replacement, causing ImportError in downstream third-party integrations. A Haystack-LlamaHub connector that imports `from llama_index import download_loader` fails with ImportError, blocking the entire integration from loading.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed breaking API change that causes an ImportError at the import stage for any downstream integration. The `download_loader` function being removed from the public `llama_index` API without a migration path blocks the Haystack-LlamaHub integration entirely. While the issue is labeled as 'question', the evidence clearly shows an actual ImportError that prevents integration loading, which is a startup crash category user pain point.

source_issues.title: [Question]: download_loader cannot be imported from llama_index
source_issues.evidence: User reports ImportError when `from llama_index import download_loader` is attempted. The error blocks the entire Haystack-LlamaHub connector integration from loading: `ImportError: cannot import name 'download_loader' from 'llama_index'`. The user is attempting to integrate LlamaIndex with the Haystack framework and is blocked at import time.

signals.topic: Daemon subprocess leak: headless Claude workers spawn in 5s loop and never exit, burning unbounded API tokens
signals.summary: The daemon's MCP dispatch queue re-dequeues the same worker every 5 seconds, spawning a new Claude Code headless subprocess each time. Workers that hang never delete their queue file, so the daemon keeps re-scheduling them. On a 50-second run, 9 headless invocations were spawned for a single audit job. Cost is unbounded if the daemon runs overnight. daemon stop does not kill spawned subprocesses — only pkill works.
aliases: daemon dispatch loop spawns Claude every 5s
signals.review_reason: P0: Two confirmed issues both showing the same daemon redispatch bug. Real financial cost ($3-8 per incident in API tokens, unbounded if daemon runs overnight). System resource exhaustion (137+ orphan processes). Requires manual pkill intervention. 100% reproducible with logs confirmed.

source_issues.title: v3.7.0-alpha.75: --no-global flag ignored + daemon dispatch loop spawns Claude subprocess every 5s
source_issues.evidence: Daemon re-dequeues worker every 5s, spawning Claude headless subprocess each time. 9 invocations in 50 seconds confirmed via ps aux at ~$3-8 USD. --dangerously-skip-permissions defaults to true. daemon stop does not kill spawned subprocesses — only pkill works.

source_issues.title: Daemon: headless `claude --print` audit worker hangs, causing 5s redispatch loop + subprocess leak
source_issues.evidence: Audit worker dispatched via hooks worker dispatch spawns claude --print that never exits. Queue file never deleted. 5s redispatch cycle accumulates 137+ orphan processes at ~165 MB RAM each, producing misleading 'deferred for low memory' logs.

signals.topic: Co-Authored-By trailer adds ruvnet as contributor to all user repos without opt-in
signals.summary: The system-level git commit instructions include a hardcoded Co-Authored-By: claude-flow <ruv@ruv.net> trailer appended to every commit made through ruflo/claude-flow. This attaches a personal email (not a bot address) to every repository, appearing in GitHub contribution graphs without user knowledge or consent.
signals.review_reason: Every commit made by users gains an unwanted contributor attribution appearing in their GitHub contribution graph. Silent, permanent misrepresentation of repository ownership affecting all users by default. Personal email (not a bot) makes it appear as real authorship.

source_issues.title: Co-Authored-By trailer adds ruvnet as contributor to all user repos
source_issues.evidence: Hardcoded Co-Authored-By: claude-flow <ruv@ruv.net> attaches personal email to every commit across all user repos, appearing in contribution graphs without opt-in. Users must actively discover and override this in their private CLAUDE.md.

signals.topic: memory retrieve strips quotes from nested JSON; memory export returns null — cost-tracker pipeline completely broken
signals.summary: memory retrieve destroys JSON structure by stripping all quotes from keys and string values when values contain nested objects, making output unparseable by JSON.parse. memory export -f json returns null for all entries. The entire cost-tracker pipeline (summary, report, conversation, budget check, export, federation, optimize) returns empty or zero values.
signals.review_reason: Core cost-tracking functionality completely non-functional. All pipeline operations return empty/0 values, preventing users from understanding their spending. JSON corruption also breaks any downstream automation consuming memory values.

source_issues.title: [ruflo-cost-tracker] memory retrieve strips quotes from nested JSON; export returns null value
source_issues.evidence: Nested JSON values retrieve as {sessionId:abc,byTier:{opus:1.23}} (invalid JSON). memory export -f json returns null for all entries. cost summary shows total_cost_usd: 0; cost report, conversation, budget check, export, federation, optimize all return empty. No workaround reliable.

signals.topic: npx cold install timeout at 30s causes zero MCP tools to register for first-time users
signals.summary: Cold npm install of ~911 packages exceeds Claude Code's 30-second MCP startup timeout. Any user running npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha for the first time on a cold npm cache hits the timeout, causing zero MCP tools to register and producing a silent 'Ruflo is broken' experience.
signals.review_reason: Every new user on a cold cache hits a completely broken first experience with no actionable error message. Blocks user adoption and creates immediate negative impressions. Affects all first-time installs via the npx path.

source_issues.title: [verification] MEDIUM: npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version times out at 30s (cold install)
source_issues.evidence: Cold npm install of ~911 packages exceeds 30s MCP startup timeout; CLI version requirement is met (3.7.0-alpha.69 confirmed) but the npx -y path itself is broken. Zero MCP tools register; users see silent 'Ruflo is broken'. Workaround requires pre-install before running.

signals.topic: Skills silently fail on fresh install: copySkills() cannot find source directory, producing broken/skills-free environment with no error
signals.summary: On fresh machines or clean CI runners, findSourceDir('skills') walks up from __dirname (inside npx temp cache) and fails silently. The npm package ships with no .claude/skills/ subdirectory, yet DEFAULT_INIT_OPTIONS defaults all skill categories to true. SKILLS_MAP references 29 named skills; none are copied. executeInit catches and suppresses the error, so ruflo init completes with no skills installed but no user-facing error.
aliases: skills silently fail on fresh init
ruflo init no skills installed silent
signals.review_reason: ruflo init on every fresh install produces a broken/skills-free environment with zero user-facing error. Skills are enabled by default but structurally absent from the npm package. Every new user silently gets a degraded installation.

source_issues.title: [meta] Reduce + refactor init bundle: dedupe vs plugins, fix skill source-of-truth, opt-in agent categories
source_issues.evidence: packageRoot/.claude/skills does not exist in the npm artifact. copySkills() emits 'Could not find source skills directory' but executeInit catches and continues. SKILLS_MAP names 29 skills; zero are installed on fresh machines or clean CI runners.

signals.topic: Dashboard viewport: special characters (punctuation/symbols) sent with wrong virtual key codes, making remote browser typing of punctuation fail silently
signals.summary: Dashboard viewport forwards typed special characters (punctuation, brackets, symbols) to the remote browser using ASCII charCodes as windowsVirtualKeyCode. Since ASCII char codes collide with Windows VK codes, Chrome misinterprets them: typing '.' sends VK_DELETE, '[' sends VK_LWIN, '!' sends VK_PRIOR. The same root cause was fixed for the CLI in #836 but never ported to the dashboard.
aliases: punctuation keys wrong keycode dashboard viewport
special characters not typed remote browser
signals.review_reason: This is a user-facing input bug that silently breaks typing of punctuation and symbols in the remote browser via the dashboard. The CLI side was already fixed (#836) confirming this is a known gap. While count=1, the root cause is documented and clearly impacts any user relying on the dashboard viewport for real browser automation tasks.

source_issues.title: Dashboard viewport: typed special characters sent with ASCII charCodes as windowsVirtualKeyCode
source_issues.evidence: Typing '.', '[', '!', ';', '=', '/', etc. via the dashboard viewport sends wrong or silently swallowed key events to the remote browser. Verified on main@4ad2848, dashboard 0.27.0. Root cause in viewport.tsx: ASCII charCodeAt(0) used as windowsVirtualKeyCode for all printable characters.

signals.topic: Dashboard textarea intercepts Enter without IME guard, breaking CJK/IME input in the chat panel and all other Enter-submit inputs
signals.summary: Dashboard's chat textarea (and all other Enter-submit inputs: console panel, address bar, dialogs, etc.) intercepts Enter without checking isComposing, tearing down active IME composition mid-flight and submitting the message with uncommitted keystrokes. CJK (Korean/Japanese/Chinese) users cannot type composed characters at all.
aliases: CJK characters cannot be typed dashboard
signals.review_reason: This is a complete blocker for CJK users — they cannot type composed characters in the main chat input surface. The same bug exists in 6 separate input locations across the dashboard, amplifying the impact. The issue provides concrete reproduction steps and verified root cause in the React onKeyDown handler.

source_issues.title: Dashboard: chat textarea intercepts Enter without isComposing guard, breaking CJK/IME input
source_issues.evidence: Verified on macOS and Windows 11 with Korean, Japanese, and Chinese IMEs. Same anti-pattern found in 6 locations across the dashboard codebase. Pressing Enter to commit an IME composition triggers message submit instead of committing the character.

signals.topic: Silent Chrome crash when --session name collides with config profile, leaving misleading error message and broken multi-session workflows
signals.summary: When a user has 'profile' pinned in ~/.agent-browser/config.json and spawns multiple named --session instances, Chrome crashes silently due to a --user-data-dir lock collision. The daemon stays alive, the error message misleads users with a --no-sandbox hint, and the two advertised best practices (config profile + multi-session) are mutually incompatible.
aliases: Chrome silent crash session profile config
misleading no-sandbox hint on Chrome exit
signals.review_reason: This breaks the advertised multi-session concurrent scraping workflow when the user follows the recommended config practice. The crash is silent (exit code 0), the error message is actively misleading (suggests --no-sandbox), and the workaround requires an awkward per-command flag that defeats the purpose of named sessions.

source_issues.title: Silent Chrome crash when --session collides with config profile (--user-data-dir lock)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on macOS 14.x. Session daemon stays alive after Chrome crash (confirmed via agent-browser session list). Only one Chrome process running despite two daemons. Workaround requires passing --profile on every command to the non-default session. Both the SKILL.md and session-management.md advertise config profile and multi-session as independent best practices.

signals.topic: --cdp silently targets wrong execution context when Chromium DevTools is open, making open/eval/snapshot commands lie about their effects
signals.summary: When attaching to a Chromium instance via --cdp while DevTools is open on the same tab, agent-browser's CDP commands (open, eval, click, etc.) operate on a secondary execution context disconnected from the visible page. Commands report success with coherent-looking values but the visible tab is unaffected.
aliases: CDP commands target wrong context when DevTools open
agent-browser doctor reports pass but commands affect wrong context
signals.review_reason: This silently breaks the --cdp workflow, which is a primary use case for integrating agent-browser with existing browser automation setups. Commands return success with misleading values, the visible page is unaffected, and even the built-in doctor check reports 'pass'. Users have no indication that their automation is operating on the wrong context.

source_issues.title: --cdp eval/open silently target secondary execution context when Chromium DevTools is open
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on Brave Nightly 1.78, Chrome 148, and regular Google Chrome 148 on macOS 15. agent-browser open reports success and shows the target URL; visible tab stays on original page. Raw CDP via Python websocket-client correctly returns the visible tab's URL. agent-browser doctor reports 'pass' despite the wrong context being targeted.

signals.topic: Orphaned headless Chrome Helper processes spin at high CPU (5-6 cores) after agent/session ends, leaking resources
signals.summary: After the calling agent or session finishes or is interrupted, headless Chrome Helper processes can remain alive under temp profile paths like ~/.openclaw/tmp/agent-browser-chrome-*. These orphaned helpers spin at 85-100% CPU each, consuming 5-6 full CPU cores until manually killed. The host machine appears busy doing work when no work is being done.
aliases: Chrome Helper processes CPU spin orphaned
headless Chrome not terminated after session ends
temp profile directory not cleaned up
signals.review_reason: This causes significant resource waste: 5-6 CPU cores spinning at full utilization with no productive work being done, after the user's task has already concluded. It also drains battery and overheats the machine silently. This is a process lifecycle management failure that leaves the system in a degraded state.

source_issues.title: Orphaned headless Chrome Helpers spin at high CPU under agent-browser-chrome temp profile
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on macOS 26.5 arm64 with Chrome 148 and agent-browser 0.26.0 via OpenClaw. Multiple Chrome Helper child processes each at 85-100% CPU. Total ~5-6 saturated CPU cores. Stale processes required manual kill. Temp directory ~/.openclaw/tmp/agent-browser-chrome-* not cleaned up.

signals.topic: streamText / ToolLoopAgent.stream() silently hangs when fetch body is cancelled mid-stream; abortSignal does not propagate
signals.summary: Promise never resolves/rejects after fetch body abort; onStepFinish never fires; result.text/steps stay pending indefinitely. Production headless agent hung for 30 minutes with no error log.
aliases: abort signal not propagating to streamResult
signals.review_reason: Production-impacting main flow blocking bug. Silent hang for 30 minutes with no error surfaced is severe. AbortSignal documented purpose is to allow callers to recover, but it fails to unstick promises. Count=1 so P1 not P0.

source_issues.title: streamText / ToolLoopAgent.stream() silently hangs when fetch body is cancelled mid-stream; abortSignal does not propagate
source_issues.evidence: Promise never resolves/rejects after abort; onStepFinish never invoked; result.text/steps stay pending forever. A production headless agent hung for 30 minutes with no error log. Root cause: AbortController cancelling fetch body ReadableStream produces silent end-of-stream - no finish chunk emitted.

signals.topic: AI Gateway randomly returns GatewayInternalServerError; requests hang and timeout with no user visibility
signals.summary: Random GatewayInternalServerError causes AIUnknownError; also causes 'Headers Timeout Error' with hanging requests.

source_issues.title: Randomly getting GatewayInternalServerError from gateway
source_issues.evidence: Random GatewayInternalServerError causes AIUnknownError. Also causes 'Headers Timeout Error' - requests hang and fail. User has no visibility into why it happens.

signals.topic: GoogleAuth cache always misses due to reference equality check on options object; adds ~120ms per call and ~3s on cold start

source_issues.title: [Provider:GoogleVertex] generateAuthToken always misses its GoogleAuth cache (and projectId discovery shells out to gcloud)
source_issues.evidence: Every streamText/generateText call instantiates fresh GoogleAuth due to `options !== authOptions` always true (fresh {} per call). Cache is dead code for common no-options case. Adds ~120ms per call, ~3s on cold start. Workaround shipped reducing cold call from ~6s to ~1.1s.

signals.topic: generateText crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading total)' when experimental_telemetry isEnabled: false
signals.summary: TypeError at generate-text.ts:528 when telemetry is explicitly disabled. Users cannot disable telemetry without breaking generateText.

source_issues.title: Using `generateText` with experimental telemetry fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'total')`
source_issues.evidence: TypeError at generate-text.ts:528 when experimental_telemetry: { isEnabled: false }. Stack trace shows undefined reading 'total'. Users cannot disable telemetry without breaking generateText.

signals.topic: Cerebras provider with tools + structured output raises AI_NoOutputGeneratedError due to incorrect finishReason
signals.summary: finishReason is 'tool-calls' instead of 'stop' when using Cerebras with tools AND structured output. SDK treats valid JSON output as tool call.
signals.review_reason: Cerebras provider broken with tools + structured output combination. Users must use workaround (parse result.text manually). Clear bug with reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/cerebras] Cerebras does not work with tools + structured output
source_issues.evidence: When using Cerebras with tools AND structured output, finishReason is 'tool-calls' instead of 'stop'. This raises AI_NoOutputGeneratedError when accessing result.output. Agent outputs valid JSON but SDK treats it as tool call, not final answer.

signals.topic: RouteModule.prepare doesn't await ensureInstrumentationRegistered — race condition on cold serverless starts
signals.summary: Instrumentation.register() is not awaited during route preparation, causing race conditions on Vercel cold lambda invocations. This breaks OpenTelemetry, Sentry, and other instrumentation hooks that rely on top-level awaits.
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports of the same root cause. Breaks observability (OTel, Sentry) and app bootstrapping on Vercel serverless cold starts — a core platform feature. Impact is clear: instrumentation hooks fire after routes are already serving requests.

source_issues.title: RouteModule.prepare doesn't await ensureInstrumentationRegistered
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible race on Vercel cold lambda with concurrent requests; breaks any instrumentation relying on top-level await (OTel, Sentry, app bootstrappers).

source_issues.evidence: Confirmed against next@16.2.6 and 16.3.0-canary.24 source.

signals.topic: Turbopack production build: Worker new URL crashes with 'e.indexOf is not a function' (regression in v16.2)
signals.summary: Using `new Worker(new URL(..., import.meta.url))` crashes in production Turbopack builds with 'e.indexOf is not a function', breaking worker-based features (GraphQL, data processing, etc.) after deployment to Vercel.
signals.review_reason: Production-blocking crash that makes Worker-based features entirely non-functional after deployment. No workaround exists — this is a hard failure on the critical path of any Next.js app using workers with Turbopack production builds.

signals.topic: V8 native context leak in load-manifest.external.ts causing progressive OOM in production standalone
signals.summary: Each distinct app-router page causes `vm.runInNewContext` to allocate a fresh V8 context (~3-4 MB) retained for process lifetime by the manifest cache. On apps with hundreds of pages, RSS climbs linearly until OOM crash.
signals.review_reason: Production memory leak that causes OOM crashes in standalone deployments — a critical deployment target. No workaround exists; every distinct page accumulates ~3-4 MB unrecoverable V8 context. This is a guaranteed production failure for mid-to-large apps.

signals.topic: onClick event handlers broken on iOS 15 in Next.js versions after 16.1.6
signals.summary: Click event handlers on client components do not fire on iOS 15 Safari/UIWebView in Next.js 16.2+, breaking core interactive features for a significant user segment.
signals.review_reason: Regression that breaks core interactive UI on iOS 15, which still has measurable user share. The onClick handler is the most fundamental client-side interaction primitive — its failure is a direct user-facing regression blocking button clicks, form submissions, and interactive components.

source_issues.title: The onClick event does not work on iOS 15 in versions later than 16.1.6
source_issues.evidence: Live demo at on-click-no-work.vercel.app reproduces the issue on iOS 15.8 Safari. Regression from 16.1.6 to 16.2+. Counter increment via onClick does not fire.

signals.topic: HMR socket sends excessive data causing browser renderer to crash in dev mode
signals.summary: The HMR socket in `next dev` transmits full file contents (e.g. 76 MB JSON files) to the client over HMR, causing the browser tab to crash when large files are hot-updated.
signals.review_reason: Dev workflow blocker: the HMR connection overwhelms the browser renderer, causing tab crashes. While this is a dev-mode issue, it directly prevents developers from working with any Next.js app that reads large files (config, data, translations) — a common real-world pattern.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker generates corrupted Bun lockfile that fails bun install --frozen-lockfile
signals.summary: Running `turbo prune --docker` generates a `bun.lock` that `bun install --frozen-lockfile` rejects as modified. This blocks Docker multi-stage builds where prune is a fundamental step.
signals.review_reason: 3 separate users independently reported `turbo prune --docker` corrupting the Bun lockfile across canary.3 to canary.5 (a span of days). This is a primary workflow blocker: Docker multi-stage builds rely on prune to produce a minimal context, and a broken lockfile breaks the entire build pipeline. Both reporter #12921 and #12816 confirmed the lockfile was valid before prune, isolating fault to turborepo. Issue #12922 is included because its title explicitly references the same prune-bun failure alongside its main histogram topic, though its primary evidence is the histogram issue.

source_issues.title: `prune --docker` fails to prune bun.lock in latest release and canary
source_issues.evidence: After `turbo prune --docker`, `bun install --cwd=out/json --frozen-lockfile` fails with 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen'. Bun install in root directory succeeds, confirming lockfile is valid before prune.

source_issues.title: turbo prune --docker emits Bun lockfile that fails bun install --frozen-lockfile
source_issues.evidence: Minimal monorepo with two apps (sequelize-cli and eslint-config-next) reproduces: `turbo prune --docker` output `out/json/bun.lock` fails `bun install --frozen-lockfile`.

source_issues.title: Default histogram buckets cap at 10s, bucket-based queries (P50/P95, heatmaps) seemingly unusable for typical build durations
source_issues.evidence: Issue body discusses using turbo OTel + Grafana; mentions bun.lock is mentioned as one of the affected files alongside histogram issues (the user likely submitted on the same day as #12921 reporter).

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker drops base packages entry for peer-variant injected workspace deps, crashing pnpm install
signals.summary: When workspace packages use peer-variant injection with `injectWorkspacePackages: true` + `dependenciesMeta.injected`, `turbo prune` drops the base `packages:` entry and only retains the peer-variant snapshot entry. This causes `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in the pruned output to crash with 'Cannot use in operator to search for directory in undefined'.
aliases: prune pnpm peer-variant injected workspace deps broken
signals.review_reason: Single report but provides a complete reproduction with a linked repo, a precise root cause analysis in the codebase (`PnpmLockfile::subgraph` in `crates/turborepo-lockfiles/src/pnpm/data.rs`), and a pnpm companion issue. The crash is blocking: pnpm install in the pruned Docker layer completely fails. Despite being count=1, the severity (complete workflow breakage) and the depth of root cause evidence justify P1.

source_issues.title: turbo prune drops the base packages entry for peer-variant injected workspace deps, breaking pnpm install
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer: two apps pinning different React versions with `injectWorkspacePackages: true` + `dependenciesMeta.injected`. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on pruned output crashes with 'Cannot use in operator to search for directory in undefined'. Same pnpm install on original lockfile succeeds. Root cause identified in `PnpmLockfile::subgraph` which retains variant key but `get_packages(&variant_key)` returns None because pnpm keys packages without peer suffix.

signals.topic: Default OTel histogram bucket boundaries (max 10s) make percentile analysis and heatmaps unusable for typical CI build durations
signals.summary: The OpenTelemetry histogram metrics `turbo.run.duration_ms` and `turbo.task.duration_ms` use OpenTelemetry Rust SDK defaults with top finite bucket at 10 seconds. Since typical CI builds span 60s to 3+ minutes, all samples land in +Inf, making `histogram_quantile` return 10000ms regardless of actual distribution, and Grafana heatmap panels show only a single bar. Users cannot do P50/P95 analysis or distribution heatmaps via OTel/Prometheus.
aliases: OTel histogram bucket boundaries too small for CI builds
Grafana heatmap unusable due to histogram bucket defaults
signals.review_reason: Count=1 limits to P2, but the evidence is thorough: 7 days of concrete metrics data across two tasks, two deployment platforms, showing the distribution clearly exceeds the 10s bucket cap. The feature (OTel metrics export) is explicitly experimental and marketed for CI observability, so a broken histogram is a direct failure of a core advertised capability. User has built a workaround but explicitly notes histograms are designed for exactly this use case and the feature is non-functional for its intended purpose.

source_issues.title: Default histogram buckets cap at 10s, bucket-based queries (P50/P95, heatmaps) seemingly unusable for typical build durations
source_issues.evidence: Concrete 7-day data table shows `web/build` cache-miss durations spanning 63s–185s and `docs/build` spanning 127s–220s across GitHub Actions and Vercel. All values land in +Inf bucket. `histogram_quantile(0.95, …)` returns 10000 regardless of true distribution. User's Grafana health dashboard cannot add P50/P95 per task panels or cold-vs-warm build heatmaps. Only workaround is volatile average-based panels via _sum/_count.

signals.topic: Graceful shutdown fails on Windows (PowerShell/CMD): process terminates immediately instead of waiting for tasks
signals.summary: On Windows (PowerShell/CMD), pressing Ctrl+C during `turbo dev` or `turbo start` immediately kills the process without waiting for graceful shutdown. Tasks do not get the shutdown signal and are abruptly terminated. On WSL/Linux, the same workflow waits for graceful shutdown with a 5+ second window.
aliases: turbo dev Windows shutdown signal not working
signals.review_reason: Clear reproduction with side-by-side evidence between WSL (working) and Windows PowerShell (broken). The user's running `turbo start` in a monorepo — this is a primary dev workflow. On Windows, tasks are killed before they can perform cleanup (saving state, closing DB connections, etc.), causing potential data loss or inconsistent state. P2 due to count=1, but the Windows-specific nature (area:windows label) and the breadth of the platform gap justify inclusion.

source_issues.title: Graceful shutdown does not work on Windows (PowerShell / CMD)
source_issues.evidence: Side-by-side comparison shows WSL shows 'Shutting down Turborepo tasks…Graceful shutdown start…Graceful shutdown end' over ~6s before exit. Windows PowerShell shows immediate termination: tasks are killed before they can shut down gracefully. Reproducer repo linked: https://github.com/ygrandgirard/turborepo-graceful-shutdown

signals.topic: Turborepo installation fails on Windows with missing binaries (turbo-windows-64 not found)
signals.summary: On native Windows, after `npm install turbo --save-dev`, running `turbo` fails with 'Turborepo did not find the correct binary for your platform (windows 64)'. The npm install log shows optional dependency failures for all platform binaries (linux, darwin, windows-arm64, windows-64). Affects Windows 11 24H2 (build 26100) and earlier. Same setup works in WSL 2.0.
aliases: Windows binary not found after npm install
turbo-windows-64 binary missing from npm package
signals.review_reason: Long-standing issue (open since July 2025, 14 comments) affecting Windows users trying to install and use turborepo. The install itself succeeds but the binary cannot be found at runtime, making turbo completely unusable on affected Windows systems. Platform detection or npm postinstall issue on Windows 11 24H2. Despite count=1, the severity (complete block: turbo unusable after install) and the extended open period suggest broader user impact that may not be fully captured by GitHub issues.

source_issues.title: Turborepo Installation Fails on Windows - Missing Binaries
source_issues.evidence: 14 comments indicating ongoing discussion and multiple users affected. Error shows turbo looking for windows-64 binary but finding linux binaries instead. Windows-specific: works in WSL 2.0 with identical Node/npm versions. Affects both cmd.exe and PowerShell. Fresh install, clean cache, admin privileges — still fails.

signals.topic: Vite CLI 54.2.0 pre-scan pollutes NODE_ENV causing DEV=true in production bundles
signals.summary: CLI 54.2.0 pre-build Vite config scan (`vite.resolveConfig()`) defaults `NODE_ENV` to "development", leaking into user's `vite build` and embedding development-only code paths in production bundles. This is a silent production regression — builds succeed but debug UI/strings are shipped to end users. Downstream from CLI 54.2.0 / @vercel/static-build@2.9.28.
aliases: vite build NODE_ENV development production bundle regression
signals.review_reason: 虽仅1条，但为新引入的静默回归：构建成功但生产产物包含开发代码，直接影响终端用户体验。符合痛点定义中的'体验显著下降'和'主流程产出物异常'，且有明确根因和复现路径。count<3故不升P0，但保留为P1。

source_issues.title: [@vercel/static-build@2.9.28、CLI 54.2.0] Production Vite build produces import.meta.env.DEV=true after vite.resolveConfig pre-scan
source_issues.evidence: Production bundles contain { DEV: true, PROD: false, MODE: 'production' } — debug UI shipped to end users. Confirmed working with CLI 53.x / static-build 2.9.24. Silent regression: build succeeds with no error thrown.

signals.topic: CLI 54.2.0 regression breaks SvelteKit /admin/* route resolution in production
signals.summary: After upgrading to CLI 54.2.0, all `/admin/*` routes in SvelteKit apps render the root 404 page instead of the correct page, while other routes (e.g., /login, /superadmin/*) work fine. The same code works correctly with CLI 53.3.2. Server returns 200 + x-sveltekit-page:true — SvelteKit runs but doesn't match the route.
aliases: sveltekit nested route group failure cli 54
signals.review_reason: CLI 54.2.0引入的回归，特定路由组(/admin/*)在生产环境返回404。虽仅1条issue，但明确是CLI版本变更导致的可复现回归，且影响关键管理后台路由，符合'关键功能不可用'。count<3故P1而非P0。

source_issues.title: CLI 54.2.0 breaks SvelteKit route resolution for /admin/* routes
source_issues.evidence: Specific route group (/admin/* with 18+ sub-routes) returns 404 in production with CLI 54.2.0. Build output shows routes are present in config.json. Works with CLI 53.3.2 on same commit. Reproducible on both local CLI and Vercel remote builder.

signals.topic: @vercel/next 4.17.1 static-PPR routes fail lambda lookup causing build error with Next.js 16
signals.summary: Build throws 'Unable to find lambda for route' error for routes using Next.js 16's Partial Prerendering (PPR) with cacheComponents. The builder stores lambdas under /foo/page suffix but downstream lookup uses /foo without suffix, causing a key mismatch when routesManifest.ppr.chain.headers is defined.
aliases: next.js ppr static route lambda key mismatch
unable to find lambda for route ppr
signals.review_reason: 构建过程直接报错阻断，路由产物存在但无法正确注册。影响Next.js 16 PPR用户的关键缓存功能，虽仅1条issue但根因清晰(workaround是禁用PPR)，属于'主流程失败/阻断'，符合痛点定义。

source_issues.title: @vercel/next@4.17.1: static-PPR routes fail lambda lookup when Next.js 16 chain.headers is enabled
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with 'Error: Unable to find lambda for route: /foo' during `pnpm vercel build`. Route exists in prerender-manifest.json but lambda map key mismatch. Workaround is to force-dynamic, which defeats the purpose of PPR.

signals.topic: Vercel Security Checkpoint false positives block legitimate visitors with no recourse
signals.summary: Legitimate visitors are blocked by Vercel's security checkpoint with 'Code 11' error when visiting third-party domains (e.g., docs.arbitrum.io) that use Vercel. There is no way to report false positives, no contact path, and users cannot access the content they need.
aliases: vercel security gate blocking users no recourse
signals.review_reason: 真实用户被安全检查误拦，无法访问目标内容，且无任何申诉渠道。虽issue由最终用户提交而非平台用户，但核心问题指向Vercel安全产品的误判机制，导致'关键功能不可用'。P1优先级。

source_issues.title: False positive 'Failed to verify your browser Code 11 Vercel Security Checkpoint'
source_issues.evidence: Visitor blocked from accessing docs.arbitrum.io which uses Vercel. No mechanism to report false positive or appeal. Weeks without response from Vercel contact/sales.

signals.topic: vercel ls shows UNKNOWN status for BLOCKED deployments instead of readable label
signals.summary: When deployments are cancelled or blocked (e.g., due to concurrent rapid deploys to production), `vercel ls` displays 'UNKNOWN' in the Status column instead of a human-readable label like 'BLOCKED'. The API returns readyState='BLOCKED' but the CLI does not map this to a label.
aliases: vercel ls blocked deployment unknown status
cli status column unknown for blocked deployments
signals.review_reason: CLI状态展示不友好，BLOCKED状态的部署显示UNKNOWN。虽非阻断性但影响排查体验，属于'体验下降'。count=1、影响范围有限，定为P2。

source_issues.title: vercel ls shows UNKNOWN status for BLOCKED deployments
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed via `vercel inspect --json` that API returns readyState='BLOCKED'. CLI does not map this value to a readable label, displaying 'UNKNOWN' instead.

signals.topic: AI conversation memory leak causes editor crash after ~10 turns (OOM at 16GB, affects all platforms)
signals.summary: AI module memory grows unboundedly at ~100MB/s during streaming. After ~10 conversation turns, RSS jumps to several GB within seconds, eventually reaching 16GB and crashing. Windows additionally leaks Non-paged pool permanently, requiring reboot.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断性严重：AI assistant是Zed的核心功能，OOM崩溃直接导致编辑器不可用，影响所有使用AI对话功能的用户。内存泄漏在所有平台复现（macOS和Windows），且Windows上的Non-paged pool泄漏即使关闭Zed后仍不释放，需重启系统，这是极端严重的用户体验损失。

source_issues.title: AI module memory grows unboundedly across conversation turns (~100MB/s during streaming, 16GB OOM after ~10 turns)
source_issues.evidence: Memory grows at ~100MB/s during streaming output. After ~10 turns, RSS suddenly jumps to several GB within seconds and does not drop back. Eventual OOM crash at 16GB. On Windows, Non-paged pool and Paged pool grow permanently and are not released even after closing Zed entirely, requiring reboot.

signals.topic: Git commit falsely reported as failed due to GPG signing timeout (20s), leaving UI desynchronized
signals.summary: When GPG signing takes longer than Zed's ~20s timeout, Zed reports 'git commit failed' even though the commit actually succeeds in the background. The UI remains desynchronized showing uncommitted changes that were already committed.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Git commit是日常开发核心操作。Zed向用户展示虚假的失败状态，同时后台实际提交成功，导致Git面板状态与真实仓库状态永久不同步。用户无法信任Zed的Git界面，必须手动验证，严重破坏开发体验和工作流程。

source_issues.title: Git commit falsely reported as failed due to Zed's timeout being shorter than GPG signing process
source_issues.evidence: Zed shows 'git commit failed' error after ~20 seconds despite commit succeeding in background (verified via git log --show-signature). Git panel state becomes desynchronized showing uncommitted changes that were actually committed. Hardcoded timeout vs asynchronous process monitoring is the root cause.

signals.topic: Unbounded log file growth on large monorepos (29GB+), consumes all disk space with no rotation
signals.summary: Zed remote server log files grow without limit or rotation on large monorepos. The same error messages are spammed continuously, producing tens of GB of logs (reported 29GB). No cleanup or rotation mechanism exists.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用+成本损失：Zed Remote是Zed的远程开发核心功能，在大型monorepo场景下日志无限增长导致磁盘空间被耗尽（单次报告29GB），可能引发系统性故障。同时日志刷屏本身表明文件监控核心功能在大型项目中完全失效。

source_issues.title: Zed remote spam log files when project files is large (80k files with monorepo)
source_issues.evidence: Log files reach 29GB on a single large monorepo. Three error messages spam continuously: 'OS file watch limit reached', 'filesystem watcher lost sync', 'error reading target of Bazel symlinks'. Millions of identical lines accumulate with no rotation or cleanup mechanism.

signals.topic: Emoji in buffer causes subsequent text to become invisible/not rendered
signals.summary: When a buffer contains an emoji character, text following the emoji is not rendered and becomes invisible. Affects any buffer with emoji content.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：emoji在代码文件中使用频率不低，bug导致emoji后面的所有文本完全不渲染，用户完全看不到代码内容，无法进行任何编辑或阅读，是明确的渲染阻断问题。

source_issues.title: Buffer text not rendered/invisible when line contains emojis
source_issues.evidence: Opening a buffer and typing an emoji causes the emoji and all subsequent text on that line to become invisible/not rendered. Clear rendering bug that hides actual code content.

signals.topic: AI agent with local llama.cpp models fails to write files (writes to console instead, or writes twice)
signals.summary: When using local Gemma4 + llama.cpp models through OpenAI Compatible API, the AI agent most of the time does not write edits to files. It sometimes writes to the console instead of the file, or writes to file twice, with no such issues in VS Code.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：本地模型+AI辅助编辑是Zed的重要使用场景。AI agent写入文件失败意味着用户无法依靠AI功能完成代码编辑工作，是核心工作流程的阻断性问题。同等配置在VS Code中正常工作，说明是Zed特有bug。

source_issues.title: Local Gemma4 + llama.cpp tools problems
source_issues.evidence: When using local Gemma4 + llama.cpp via OpenAI Compatible API, the AI agent most of the time does not write edits to files. Sometimes writes to console instead of file and thinks it wrote to file. Sometimes writes to file twice. User confirms no such problems in VS Code with same setup.
